title.zh: 卷一百五十五 列傳第四十二: 汪世顯 史天澤
title.en: Volume 155 Biographies 42: Wang Shixian, Shi Tianze
title.raw: 卷一百五十五 列傳第四十二: 汪世顯 史天澤 Volume 155 Biographies 42: Wang Shixian, Shi Tianze

sentences.zh: 汪世顯德臣 良臣 惟正

translations.literal: Wang Shixian; Dechen; Liangchen; Weizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shixian; [his sons] Dechen, Liangchen, and Weizheng.

sentences.zh: 汪世顯字仲明，鞏昌鹽川人。

translations.literal: Wang Shixian, courtesy name Zhongming, was a native of Yanchuan in Gongchang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shixian, whose courtesy name was Zhongming, came from Yanchuan in Gongchang.

sentences.zh: 系出旺古族。

translations.literal: His lineage came from the Wanggu tribe.
translations.idiomatic: He was descended from the Wanggu people.

sentences.zh: 仕金，屢立戰功，官至鎮遠軍節度使，鞏昌便宜緫帥。

translations.literal: He served the Jin, repeatedly distinguished himself in battle, and rose to Military Commissioner of the Zhenyuan Army and Regional Commander of Gongchang with discretionary powers.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Jin dynasty, won repeated victories, and eventually became military commissioner of the Zhenyuan Army and regional commander of Gongchang with full discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 金平，郡縣望風款附，世顯獨城守，及皇子闊端駐兵城下，始率衆降。

translations.literal: When the Jin fell, prefectures and counties submitted at the first news; Shixian alone held the city. Only when Prince Kuoduan encamped beneath the walls did he lead the masses in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin collapsed, counties and prefectures surrendered as soon as they heard the news, but Shixian alone held his city. Not until Prince Kuoduan had encamped beneath the walls did he lead his people out to submit.

sentences.zh: 皇子曰：「吾征四方，所至皆下，汝獨固守，何也？」

translations.literal: The prince said, "I campaign in the four quarters and everywhere submits; you alone held fast—why?"
translations.idiomatic: The prince said, "I campaign across the realm and every place I reach surrenders—why did you alone hold out?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣不敢背主失節耳。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Your servant dared not betray his lord and lose his integrity."
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I could not bring myself to betray my sovereign and abandon my duty."

sentences.zh: 又問曰：「金亡已久，汝不降，果誰為耶？」

translations.literal: He asked again, "Jin has long been extinct; whom were you holding out for, in the end?"
translations.idiomatic: The prince asked again, "The Jin have been gone for ages—who exactly were you still holding the city for?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「大軍迭至，莫知適從，惟殿下仁武不殺，竊意必能保全闔城軍民，是以降也。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Great armies came in succession and one knew not whom to follow. Only Your Highness is benevolent and martial and does not slaughter; I privately believed you could certainly preserve the soldiers and civilians of the whole city—therefore I submitted."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Armies kept arriving one after another, and we did not know whom to obey. I believed that Your Highness, being both merciful and formidable and sparing lives, would surely be able to protect everyone in the city—that is why I surrendered."

sentences.zh: 皇子大悅，承制錫世顯章服，官從其舊。

translations.literal: The prince was greatly pleased and, by imperial commission, bestowed ceremonial robes on Shixian; his office remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was delighted. Acting on imperial authority, he granted Shixian court robes and let him keep his former rank.

sentences.zh: 即從南征，斷嘉陵，擣大安。

translations.literal: He then followed the southern campaign, severed Jialing, and stormed Da'an.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined the southern campaign, cut the Jialing route, and assaulted Da'an.

sentences.zh: 田、楊諸蠻結陣迎敵，世顯以輕騎馳撓之。

translations.literal: The Tian, Yang, and other barbarian tribes formed battle lines to meet the enemy; Shixian with light cavalry galloped to harass them.
translations.idiomatic: The Tian, Yang, and other tribal forces drew up in battle array; Shixian harried them with light cavalry raids.

sentences.zh: 宋曹將軍潛兵相為掎角，世顯單騎突之，殺數十人。

translations.literal: Song General Cao deployed hidden troops in mutual support; Shixian charged them alone on horseback and killed several tens of men.
translations.idiomatic: The Song general Cao had concealed troops working in concert from two sides; Shixian charged in alone and killed dozens of men.

sentences.zh: 黎明，大軍四合，殺其主將，入武信，遂進逼資、普。

translations.literal: At dawn the great army closed in from four sides, killed their commander, entered Wuxin, and then pressed on toward Zi and Pu.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak the main force closed in from all sides, killed the enemy commander, took Wuxin, and advanced against Zizhou and Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 軍葭萌，宋將依山為柵，世顯以數騎往奪之，乘勝定資州，略嘉定、峨眉。

translations.literal: The army reached Jiameng; a Song general built stockades along the mountain; Shixian with a few horsemen went to seize them, and following victory secured Zizhou and overran Jiading and Emei.
translations.idiomatic: The army reached Jiameng, where a Song commander had built mountain stockades; Shixian took them with a handful of horsemen, then pressed the advantage to secure Zizhou and overrun Jiading and Emei.

sentences.zh: 進次開州。

translations.literal: He advanced and encamped at Kaizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced and made camp at Kaizhou.

sentences.zh: 時方泥潦，由間道攀緣以達。

translations.literal: At the time the roads were muddy and flooded; he climbed along bypaths to reach it.
translations.idiomatic: The season was one of mud and flood; he reached the place by clambering along mountain paths.

sentences.zh: 宋軍屯萬州南岸，世顯即水北造船以疑之，夜從上游鼓革舟襲破之，宋師大擾，追奔至夔峽，過巫山，與宋援軍遇，斬首三千餘級。

translations.literal: Song troops were encamped on the south bank of Wanzhou; Shixian immediately built boats north of the water to deceive them, and at night from upstream drummed and attacked with leather boats, breaking them. The Song army was greatly thrown into disorder; pursuit ran to Kuixia, passed Wushan, met Song relief troops, and beheaded more than three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Song forces held the south bank at Wanzhou; Shixian built decoy boats on the north shore, then at night attacked from upstream with drumming and leather-hulled craft and routed them. The Song army fell into chaos; he pursued as far as the Kuixia Gorge, crossed Wushan, met Song reinforcements, and took more than three thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 明年，師還攻重慶，會大暑，乃罷歸。

translations.literal: The next year the army returned to attack Chongqing; encountering great heat, they then ceased and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the army returned to attack Chongqing, but the fierce summer heat forced them to break off and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 覲太宗，錫金符，易其名曰中山，且歷數其功，世顯拜謝曰：「此皆聖明福德所致，臣何預焉！」

translations.literal: He had an audience with Emperor Taizong, who bestowed a gold tally, changed his name to Zhongshan, and enumerated his achievements. Shixian bowed in thanks and said, "All this is due to Your Sagely brilliance and good fortune—what part had your servant in it!"
translations.idiomatic: He presented himself to Emperor Taizong (Ögedei), who granted him a gold tally, renamed him Zhongshan, and recounted his deeds. Shixian bowed and said, "That is all the fruit of Your Majesty's wisdom and fortune—what credit is mine?"

sentences.zh: 辛丑，蜀帥陳隆之貽書請戰，聲言有衆百萬，皇子集諸將議之，咸謂隆之可生擒也。

translations.literal: In the xinchou year, Shu commander Chen Longzhi sent a letter requesting battle, claiming a force of a million. The prince gathered the generals to discuss it; all said Longzhi could be taken alive.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinchou year, the Song commander of Shu, Chen Longzhi, sent a challenge boasting a million men. The prince called his generals together; all agreed that Longzhi could be captured alive.

sentences.zh: 世顯曰：「顧臨敵何如，無庸誇辭為！」

translations.literal: Shixian said, "Just see how he fares when facing the enemy—no need for boastful words!"
translations.idiomatic: Shixian said, "Let us see how he fights when we meet—there is no need for all this boasting!"

sentences.zh: 軍薄成都，隆之戰屢却，堅壁不出。

translations.literal: The army pressed close to Chengdu; Longzhi fought repeatedly and was driven back, then held the walls and would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: The army closed on Chengdu; Longzhi was beaten back in several engagements and then shut himself behind the walls.

sentences.zh: 其部曲田顯約夜降，降之覺之，世顯曰：「事急矣！」

translations.literal: His subordinate Tian Xian arranged a night surrender; Longzhi discovered it. Shixian said, "The matter is urgent!"
translations.idiomatic: One of his officers, Tian Xian, had arranged to defect by night, but Longzhi found out. Shixian cried, "This is urgent!"

sentences.zh: 亟梯城入救顯，得與從者七十餘人出，獲隆之，斬之。

translations.literal: He hastily scaled the wall on ladders to rescue Xian, got out with more than seventy followers, captured Longzhi, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He scaled the city wall at once to rescue Xian, brought out more than seventy of his men, seized Longzhi, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 世顯復簡精銳五百人，擣漢州，州兵三千出戰，城閉，盡沒。

translations.literal: Shixian again selected five hundred elite troops and stormed Hanzhou; three thousand prefectural troops came out to fight; the city gates were shut and all were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Shixian picked five hundred crack troops and assaulted Hanzhou; three thousand local defenders sallied out, the gates were shut behind them, and every man was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 三日，大軍薄其城，又三日，克之。

translations.literal: In three days the great army pressed the city; in three more days it was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later the main army reached the city; three days after that it fell.

sentences.zh: 癸卯春，皇子第功，承制拜便宜緫帥，秦、鞏等二十餘州事皆聽裁決，賜虎符、錦衣、玉帶。

translations.literal: In spring of the guimao year the prince ranked his achievements; by commission he was appointed Regional Commander with discretionary powers; affairs of more than twenty prefectures including Qin and Gong were all subject to his decision; he was granted a tiger tally, brocade robes, and a jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of guimao the prince graded his merits and, by imperial commission, made him regional commander with full discretion over more than twenty prefectures including Qin and Gongchang, granting him a tiger tally, brocade robes, and a jade belt.

sentences.zh: 世顯先已遘疾，至是加劇，皇子遣醫，絡繹往療，竟不起，年四十九。

translations.literal: Shixian had already fallen ill; now it worsened. The prince sent physicians who came in an unbroken stream to treat him, but he could not recover; he was forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Shixian had already been ill, and now his condition worsened. The prince sent physicians in steady succession, but he did not recover; he was forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 中統三年，論功追封隴西公，諡義武。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong, his merits were reviewed and he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Longxi, with the posthumous name Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhongtong (1262) his services were recognized and he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Longxi, with the temple name Yiwu (Loyal and Martial).

sentences.zh: 延祐七年，加封隴右王。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yanyou he was further enfeoffed as Prince of Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yanyou (1320) he was further elevated to Prince of Longyou.

sentences.zh: 子七人：忠臣，鞏昌便宜副緫帥；

translations.literal: He had seven sons: Zhongchen, Deputy Regional Commander of Gongchang with discretionary powers;
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons: Zhongchen, deputy regional commander of Gongchang;

sentences.zh: 次德臣；

translations.literal: next Dechen;
translations.idiomatic: next, Dechen;

sentences.zh: 次直臣，鞏昌中路都緫領，歿於王事；

translations.literal: next Zhichen, Chief Commander of the Middle Route of Gongchang, who died in the king's service;
translations.idiomatic: next Zhichen, chief commander of the middle route at Gongchang, who died on campaign;

sentences.zh: 次良臣；

translations.literal: next Liangchen;
translations.idiomatic: next, Liangchen;

sentences.zh: 次翰臣，奧魯兵馬都元帥；

translations.literal: next Hanchen, Grand Marshal of the Örüg Army;
translations.idiomatic: next Hanchen, grand marshal of the örüg forces;

sentences.zh: 佐臣，鞏昌左翼都緫領，歿於王事；

translations.literal: Zuochen, Chief Commander of the Left Wing of Gongchang, who died in the king's service;
translations.idiomatic: Zuochen, chief commander of the left wing at Gongchang, who died on campaign;

sentences.zh: 清臣，四川行樞密院副使。

translations.literal: Qingchen, Vice Commissioner of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat for Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: and Qingchen, vice commissioner of the Sichuan branch secretariat for military affairs.

sentences.zh: 德臣，賜名田哥，字舜輔。

translations.literal: Dechen was granted the name Tiange, courtesy name Shunfu.
translations.idiomatic: Dechen was given the Mongol name Tiange; his courtesy name was Shunfu.

sentences.zh: 年十四，侍太子游獵，矢無虛發。

translations.literal: At fourteen he attended the crown prince on the hunt; not an arrow missed.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he accompanied the crown prince on a hunt and never missed a shot.

sentences.zh: 襲爵鞏昌等二十四路便宜都緫帥，從征蜀，將前軍出忠、涪，所向克獲。

translations.literal: He inherited the title of Regional Commander with discretionary powers over the twenty-four routes including Gongchang, followed the campaign in Shu, led the vanguard out from Zhong and Fu, and wherever he went gained victory and booty.
translations.idiomatic: He inherited his father's post as regional commander over twenty-four circuits including Gongchang, joined the Shu campaign, led the vanguard through Zhongzhou and Fuzhou, and carried every objective he attacked.

sentences.zh: 進攻運山，率麾下先，所乘馬中飛石死，步戰，拔外城。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Yunshan, he led his men in the van; the horse he rode was killed by a flying stone; he fought on foot and took the outer city.
translations.idiomatic: Attacking Yunshan, he led from the front; his horse was killed by a catapult stone, so he fought on foot and stormed the outer wall.

sentences.zh: 宋將餘玠攻漢中，德臣馳赴之，玠聞，遁去。

translations.literal: Song general Yu Jie attacked Hanzhong; Dechen galloped to the rescue; when Jie heard, he fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song general Yu Jie attacked Hanzhong, Dechen rode to the relief; Jie withdrew as soon as he heard Dechen was coming.

sentences.zh: 憲宗素聞其名，及入覲，所陳悉嘉納，賜印符，命城沔州。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong had long heard his name; when he came to audience, everything he presented was praised and accepted; he was granted a seal tally and ordered to fortify Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Möngke had long known his reputation; at his audience everything Dechen proposed was approved, he received an official seal, and was ordered to build up Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 沔據嘉陵要路，德臣繕治室廬，部署官屬，數日而集。

translations.literal: Mizhou held the vital route of Jialing; Dechen repaired dwellings, deployed officials, and in a few days all was gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Mizhou commanded the vital Jialing corridor; Dechen put up buildings, posted his staff, and had the place organized within days.

sentences.zh: 進攻嘉定，敵潛軍夜出，德臣迎戰，殺百人。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Jiading, the enemy sent hidden troops out by night; Dechen met them in battle and killed a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: During the assault on Jiading the enemy sortied by night with concealed troops; Dechen met them and killed a hundred men.

sentences.zh: 還至左綿雲頂，宋軍乘夜斫營，覺之，殺千人，生擒百人。

translations.literal: Returning to Yunding in Zuomian, Song troops by night raided the camp; he detected them, killed a thousand, and took a hundred alive.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to Yunding in Zuomian, Song forces raided the camp at night; he caught them in the act, killed a thousand, and took a hundred prisoners.

sentences.zh: 進次隆慶，宋軍仍夜出，與力戰，盡殺之。

translations.literal: He advanced and encamped at Longqing; Song troops again came out by night; he fought them fiercely and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: He moved on to Longqing; the Song again attacked by night; he fought them hand to hand and wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 及馬漕溝，遇伏兵，與戰，獲其統制羅廷鶚。

translations.literal: At Macao Gully he met ambush troops, fought them, and captured their commander Luo Ting'e.
translations.idiomatic: At Macao Gully he ran into an ambush, defeated it, and captured the Song commander Luo Ting'e.

sentences.zh: 又詔德臣城益昌，諸戍皆聽節制。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to fortify Yichang; all garrisons were to obey his command.
translations.idiomatic: He was further ordered to fortify Yichang, with every garrison placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 世祖以皇弟有事西南，德臣入見，乞免益昌賦稅及徭役漕糧，屯田為長久計，並從之。

translations.literal: Shizu, as imperial younger brother, had business in the southwest; Dechen came to audience and begged exemption of Yichang from taxes, corvée, and transport grain, with garrison farming as a long-term plan—all was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai, then still a prince with affairs in the southwest, received Dechen, who asked that Yichang be freed from taxes, labor levies, and grain transport dues and that garrison farms be established for the long term; all was approved.

sentences.zh: 即命置行部于鞏，立漕司于沔，通販鬻，給餽餉。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered a traveling office set up at Gong, a transport bureau established at Mian, trade opened for sale, and provisions supplied.
translations.idiomatic: He at once set up a field headquarters at Gongchang, a grain transport office at Mizhou, opened trade, and secured supplies.

sentences.zh: 奏乞以兄忠臣攝府事，使己得專事益昌。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking that his elder brother Zhongchen administer the prefectural affairs so that he himself could devote himself solely to Yichang.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that his elder brother Zhongchen run the prefectural administration so that he could focus entirely on Yichang.

sentences.zh: 益昌為蜀喉襟，蜀人憚其威名，諸郡環視，莫敢出鬪。

translations.literal: Yichang was the throat and breastwork of Shu; the people of Shu feared his martial renown; the surrounding prefectures looked on from all sides and none dared come out to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Yichang was the gateway to Shu; the Song feared his name, and the surrounding prefectures watched from the sidelines without daring to give battle.

sentences.zh: 甲寅春，旱，嘉陵漕舟水澀，議者欲棄去，德臣曰：「國家以蜀事託我，有死而已，奈何棄之！」

translations.literal: In spring of the jiayin year there was drought; Jialing transport boats were stranded in shallow water; advisers wished to abandon them. Dechen said, "The state has entrusted me with Shu affairs—death is all there is; how could I abandon them!"
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of jiayin a drought left the Jialing grain boats stranded; some urged abandoning them. Dechen said, "The court has entrusted the Shu campaign to me—I can only die in place; how could I walk away from this?"

sentences.zh: 盡殺所乘馬饗士。

translations.literal: He killed all the horses he rode and feasted the troops with them.
translations.idiomatic: He slaughtered every horse in his train to feed the men.

sentences.zh: 襲嘉川，得糧二千餘石。

translations.literal: He raided Jiazhou and obtained more than two thousand piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He raided Jiazhou and seized more than two thousand piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 雲頂呂達將兵五千邀戰，即陣擒之，復得糧五千石。

translations.literal: At Yunding, Lü Da led five thousand troops to intercept battle; Dechen seized him on the field at once and again obtained five thousand piculs of grain.
translations.idiomatic: At Yunding, Lü Da brought five thousand men to block him; Dechen captured him in the field and took another five thousand piculs of grain.

sentences.zh: 既而魚關、金牛水陸運偕至，屯田麥亦登，食用遂給。

translations.literal: Before long transport by water and land from Yuguan and Jinniu arrived together; garrison-field wheat also ripened, and food and supplies were thus provided.
translations.idiomatic: Soon supplies arrived by both land and water from Yuguan and Jinniu, the garrison wheat ripened, and provisions were secure.

sentences.zh: 夏，獲宋提轄崔忠、鄭再立，縱令持檄諭苦竹，守將南清以城降，所俘城中民，悉歸之。

translations.literal: In summer he captured Song commissioners Cui Zhong and Zheng Zaili, released them to carry proclamations to persuade Kuzhu; the defending general Nan Qing surrendered the city; all civilians taken in the city were returned to them.
translations.idiomatic: That summer he captured the Song commissioners Cui Zhong and Zheng Zaili and sent them with surrender notices to Kuzhu; the defender Nan Qing yielded the city, and every civilian taken there was returned unharmed.

sentences.zh: 東南戍卒數百有去志，德臣揣知之，給券縱去，皆泣謝。

translations.literal: Several hundred southeast garrison troops wished to leave; Dechen perceived it, gave them passes and let them go; all wept in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred southeastern garrison troops wanted to desert; Dechen understood, issued them safe-conduct, and let them go; they left in tears, thanking him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，山寨相繼輸款。

translations.literal: Before long mountain stockades submitted tribute in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the mountain strongholds surrendered one after another.

sentences.zh: 宋將餘晦遣都統甘閏，以兵數萬城紫金山，德臣即選精卒，銜枚夜進，大破之，閏僅以身免。

translations.literal: Song general Yu Hui sent Commander Gan Run with tens of thousands of troops to fortify Zijin Mountain; Dechen immediately chose elite troops, advanced by night with gags in their mouths, and routed them greatly; Run barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: The Song general Yu Hui sent the commander Gan Run with tens of thousands of men to fortify Mount Zijin; Dechen chose elite troops, attacked silently by night, and routed them; Gan Run barely escaped alive.

sentences.zh: 南清北覲，其下殺清妻子以叛，蜀將焦遠領兵餉之，德臣擊敗遠，盡獲所餉資糧。

translations.literal: Nan Qing went north to audience; his subordinates killed Qing's wife and children in rebellion; Shu general Jiao Yuan led troops to supply them; Dechen defeated Yuan and seized all the supplies and grain he was bringing.
translations.idiomatic: Nan Qing went north to court; his men murdered his wife and children and rebelled; the Shu general Jiao Yuan marched to support them; Dechen defeated Yuan and captured all his supplies.

sentences.zh: 冬，蜀兵二萬復至，又敗之，獲糧百餘艘。

translations.literal: In winter twenty thousand Shu troops came again; he defeated them again and captured more than a hundred grain boats.
translations.idiomatic: In winter twenty thousand Shu troops returned; he beat them again and took more than a hundred grain boats.

sentences.zh: 魚關至沔水，迂回為渡百有八，至是，悉為橋梁。

translations.literal: From Yuguan to the Mian River the winding route had one hundred and eight fords; by this time all were bridged.
translations.idiomatic: Between Yuguan and the Mian River the winding route had 108 fords; by now he had bridged every one of them.

sentences.zh: 戊午歲，帝親征，次漢中，德臣朝行在所。

translations.literal: In the wuwu year the emperor campaigned in person, halted at Hanzhong; Dechen had audience at the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuwu year the emperor led the campaign in person and halted at Hanzhong; Dechen presented himself at the field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 初，諸路軍成都，猝為宋人所圍，德臣遣將赴之，約曰：「先破敵者，奏領此城。」

translations.literal: Earlier, armies of all routes were at Chengdu and were suddenly surrounded by Song men; Dechen sent a general to the rescue with the agreement: "Whoever first breaks the enemy shall memorialize to receive this city."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the combined armies had reached Chengdu when Song forces suddenly surrounded them; Dechen sent a relief column under the pledge that whoever broke the siege first would be granted the city.

sentences.zh: 圍遂解。

translations.literal: The siege was then lifted.
translations.idiomatic: The siege was lifted.

sentences.zh: 詔候江南事定，如約以城與之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that when affairs south of the Yangtze were settled, the city should be given him as agreed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promised that once the south was pacified, the city would be his as pledged.

sentences.zh: 帝幸益昌，駐北山，謂德臣曰：「來者言汝立利州之功，今見汝身甚小，而膽甚大，不知敵曾薄汝城否？」

translations.literal: The emperor visited Yichang and encamped on North Mountain, saying to Dechen, "Those who came said you achieved merit at Lizhou; now I see your person is very small yet your courage very great—I wonder whether the enemy has ever pressed your city?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor visited Yichang and camped on North Mountain. He said to Dechen, "Reports say you won Lizhou; I see you are slight of build but bold in spirit—have the enemy ever pressed your walls?"

sentences.zh: 德臣對曰：「賴陛下洪福，未嘗一來。」

translations.literal: Dechen replied, "Relying on Your Majesty's vast good fortune, they have never come once."
translations.idiomatic: Dechen answered, "By Your Majesty's good fortune, not once."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「彼憚卿威名耳。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "They fear your martial renown, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "They fear your name, that is all."

sentences.zh: 賜金帶，且俾立石紀功。

translations.literal: He was granted a gold belt and moreover ordered to erect a stone to record his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He was given a gold belt and ordered to set up a stone monument to his deeds.

sentences.zh: 嘉陵、白水交會，勢洶急，帝問：「船幾何可濟？」

translations.literal: Where Jialing and Baishui meet the current is fierce and swift; the emperor asked, "How many boats can cross?"
translations.idiomatic: At the confluence of the Jialing and Baishui the current runs fierce; the emperor asked, "How many boats would it take to cross?"

sentences.zh: 德臣曰：「大軍百萬，非可淹延，當別為方略。」

translations.literal: Dechen said, "An army of a million cannot be delayed; another plan must be made."
translations.idiomatic: Dechen said, "A host of a million cannot wait—we need another plan."

sentences.zh: 即命繫舟為梁，一夕而成，如履坦途。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered boats lashed into a bridge; in one night it was done, like walking a level road.
translations.idiomatic: He had boats lashed into a bridge that was finished overnight, solid as a paved road.

sentences.zh: 帝顧謂諸王曰：「汪德臣言不虛發。」

translations.literal: The emperor turned and said to the princes, "Wang Dechen's words are not spoken in vain."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to the princes and said, "Wang Dechen does not boast idly."

sentences.zh: 賜白金三十斤，仍命刻石紀功。

translations.literal: He was granted thirty jin of white gold and again ordered to carve stone recording his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: He was given thirty jin of silver and again ordered to inscribe his deeds on stone.

sentences.zh: 苦竹既逆命，至是攻之，巖壁峭絕，或請建天橋，帝以問德臣，曰：「臣知先登陷陣而已，建橋非所知也。」

translations.literal: Kuzhu had already defied orders; now they attacked it; cliffs and walls were precipitous and sheer; some asked to build a sky bridge. The emperor questioned Dechen, who said, "Your servant knows only leading the assault and breaking the ranks; building bridges is not what I know."
translations.idiomatic: Kuzhu had rebelled; now they assaulted it, where the cliffs were sheer. Some proposed a flying bridge; the emperor asked Dechen, who said, "I know only how to lead the charge—I know nothing of building bridges."

sentences.zh: 既而橋果無功。

translations.literal: Before long the bridge indeed achieved nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The bridge, as it turned out, failed.

sentences.zh: 乃率將士魚貫而進，帝望見，歎曰：「人言其膽勇，豈虛譽邪！」

translations.literal: He then led officers and troops in single file to advance; the emperor saw and sighed, "Men say his courage is bold—can it be empty praise!"
translations.idiomatic: He led his men up in single file; the emperor watched and exclaimed, "They say he is fearless—no empty reputation!"

sentences.zh: 宋將趙仲武納款，而楊禮猶拒戰，奮擊，盡殺之。

translations.literal: Song general Zhao Zhongwu submitted allegiance, but Yang Li still resisted battle; Dechen struck fiercely and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: The Song general Zhao Zhongwu surrendered, but Yang Li still fought on; Dechen attacked fiercely and killed them to the last man.

sentences.zh: 德臣微疾，帝勞之曰：「汝疾皆為我家。」

translations.literal: Dechen had a slight illness; the emperor comforted him, saying, "Your illness is all for our house."
translations.idiomatic: Dechen had fallen slightly ill; the emperor comforted him: "Your sickness is all for our family's sake."

sentences.zh: 飲以葡萄酒，解玉帶賜之，曰：「飲我酒，服我帶，疾其有瘳乎！」

translations.literal: He gave him wine to drink, removed his jade belt and bestowed it, saying, "Drink my wine, wear my belt—will not the illness have recovery!"
translations.idiomatic: He gave him wine, took off his own jade belt and bestowed it, and said, "Drink my wine and wear my belt—surely you will recover!"

sentences.zh: 德臣泣謝。

translations.literal: Dechen wept in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Dechen wept as he thanked him.

sentences.zh: 宋龍州守將王德新，遣所親願效順，以郡民為祈，奏如其請。

translations.literal: Song defending general of Longzhou Wang Dexin sent a close associate wishing to submit allegiance, pleading on behalf of the prefectural people; a memorial was submitted granting the request as asked.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dexin, the Song defender of Longzhou, sent a trusted envoy offering surrender and begging mercy for the people; Dechen memorialized and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 進攻長寧，拔之，斬守將王佐。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Changning, took it, and beheaded the defending general Wang Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Changning, took it, and executed the defender Wang Zuo.

sentences.zh: 帝東下，德臣為先鋒，抵大獲山，奪水門。

translations.literal: The emperor went east; Dechen was vanguard, reached Dahuoshan, and seized the water gate.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor marched east, Dechen led the vanguard to Dahuoshan and seized the water gate.

sentences.zh: 宋將楊大淵遣子乞活數萬人命。

translations.literal: Song general Yang Dayuan sent his son to beg the lives of tens of thousands of men.
translations.idiomatic: The Song general Yang Dayuan sent his son to plead for the lives of tens of thousands of men.

sentences.zh: 引至帝前為請，旦日，大淵率衆降。

translations.literal: Dechen led him before the emperor to plead; at dawn the next day Dayuan led the masses in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Dechen brought him before the emperor to make the plea; the next morning Dayuan surrendered with his troops.

sentences.zh: 已而運山、青居、大梁皆降。

translations.literal: Before long Yunshan, Qingju, and Daliang all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yunshan, Qingju, and Daliang all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 攻釣魚山，守臣王堅負險，五月不下，德臣單騎至城下，大呼曰：「王堅，我來活汝一城軍民，宜早降！」

translations.literal: They attacked Diaoyushan; the defender Wang Jian relied on perilous terrain; for five months it would not fall. Dechen alone on horseback came to beneath the walls and shouted loudly, "Wang Jian, I have come to give life to your whole city's soldiers and civilians—you should submit early!"
translations.idiomatic: They besieged Diaoyu Fortress, where Wang Jian held the heights; after five months it still stood. Dechen rode alone to the foot of the wall and shouted, "Wang Jian, I have come to spare your city—surrender now!"

sentences.zh: 語未既，幾為飛石所中，遂感疾。

translations.literal: Before the words were finished he was nearly struck by a flying stone and thus fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely finished speaking when a catapult stone nearly struck him; he fell ill from the shock.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使問勞，俾還益昌，奏曰：「陛下尊為天子，猶冒寒暑，服勞于外，臣侍罪行伍，死其分也。」

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to inquire after him and ordered him back to Yichang. He memorialized, "Your Majesty, honored as Son of Heaven, still braves heat and cold and labors abroad; your servant attends in the ranks—death is his portion."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to inquire after him and ordered him back to Yichang. He memorialized, "Your Majesty is emperor, yet you still brave heat and cold on campaign; I am only a soldier in your ranks—to die is my duty."

sentences.zh: 又遣丞相兀真賜湯劑，卒不起，年三十有六。

translations.literal: He again sent Chancellor Wuzhen to bestow medicinal broth; in the end he could not recover; he was thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also sent the chancellor Wuzhen with medicine, but Dechen did not recover; he was thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 中統三年，追封隴西公，諡忠烈。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Longxi, with the posthumous name Zhonglie.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhongtong (1262) he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Longxi, with the temple name Zhonglie (Loyal and Ardent).

sentences.zh: 子六人；

translations.literal: He had six sons;
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons:

sentences.zh: 長惟正；

translations.literal: the eldest Weizheng;
translations.idiomatic: the eldest, Weizheng;

sentences.zh: 次惟賢，大司徒；

translations.literal: next Weixian, Grand Preceptor;
translations.idiomatic: next Weixian, grand preceptor;

sentences.zh: 惟和，昭文館大學士；

translations.literal: Weihe, Grand Academician of the Zhaowen Hall;
translations.idiomatic: Weihe, grand academician of the Zhaowen Hall;

sentences.zh: 惟明，以質子為元帥；

translations.literal: Weiming, served as marshal while a hostage;
translations.idiomatic: Weiming, who served as marshal while held as a hostage;

sentences.zh: 惟能，征西都元帥；

translations.literal: Weineng, Grand Marshal of the Western Campaign;
translations.idiomatic: Weineng, grand marshal of the western campaign;

sentences.zh: 惟純，權便宜都總帥。

translations.literal: Weichun, Acting Regional Commander with discretionary powers.
translations.idiomatic: and Weichun, acting regional commander with discretionary authority.

sentences.zh: 良臣，年十六七即從兄德臣出征。

translations.literal: Liangchen, at sixteen or seventeen already followed his elder brother Dechen on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Liangchen, at sixteen or seventeen, already followed his brother Dechen on campaign.

sentences.zh: 每戰輒當前鋒，以功擢裨帥，兼便宜都府參議。

translations.literal: In every battle he always took the vanguard; for merit he was promoted to deputy commander and concurrently served as councilor of the discretionary commandery office.
translations.idiomatic: In every battle he led the van; for his deeds he was made deputy commander and councilor on the regional staff.

sentences.zh: 癸丑歲，以德臣薦，為鞏昌帥，領所部兵屯田白水，蜀邊寨不敢復出鈔略。

translations.literal: In the guichou year, on Dechen's recommendation, he became commander of Gongchang, led his troops in garrison farming at Baishui, and Shu border stockades did not dare again come out to raid.
translations.idiomatic: In guichou, on Dechen's recommendation, he became commander of Gongchang, garrisoned his men at Baishui for farming, and the Song border forts ceased their raids.

sentences.zh: 憲宗親征，軍至六盤，良臣還鞏昌，供億所須，事集而民不擾，詔權便宜緫帥府事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong campaigned in person, the army reached Liupan; Liangchen returned to Gongchang and supplied all needs; affairs were gathered yet the people were not disturbed; he was ordered to act as regional commander with discretionary powers over prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Möngke campaigned in person and reached Liupan, Liangchen returned to Gongchang, furnished all supplies without disturbing the people, and was authorized to act as regional commander.

sentences.zh: 良臣奏：「願與兄德臣效力定四川。」

translations.literal: Liangchen memorialized, "I wish to join my elder brother Dechen in exerting strength to pacify Sichuan."
translations.idiomatic: Liangchen memorialized, "I wish to serve with my brother Dechen to pacify Sichuan."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「行軍餽餉，所係不輕，汝任其責，自可立功。」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "March provisions and transport are no light matter; if you bear that responsibility, you may yourself achieve merit."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Army supply is no small matter; take that charge and you will earn merit of your own."

sentences.zh: 良臣既奉命，治橋梁，平道路，營舟車，水陸無壅，儲積充牣。

translations.literal: Liangchen, having received the command, repaired bridges, leveled roads, and organized boats and carts; by water and land nothing was blocked, and stores were full.
translations.idiomatic: Once commissioned, Liangchen repaired bridges, cleared roads, and organized transport by land and water until supplies were abundant.

sentences.zh: 有旨賜黃金、弓矢，旌其能。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed gold and bow and arrows, commending his ability.
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted him gold, bow, and arrows in recognition of his service.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，阿藍台兒、渾都海逆命，劫六盤府庫，西垂騷動，詔良臣討之。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, Alantai'er and Hunduhai defied orders, plundered the Liupan treasury, and the western border was in turmoil; Liangchen was ordered to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When Kublai came to the throne, Alantai'er and Hunduhai rebelled, looted the Liupan treasury, and threw the western frontier into disorder; Liangchen was ordered to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 兵至山丹，置營，按兵不戰者凡二月。

translations.literal: The army reached Shandan and encamped; he held his troops without fighting for two months in all.
translations.idiomatic: His army reached Shandan and encamped, holding back from battle for two full months.

sentences.zh: 俄大舉至耀碑谷，兩軍相當，良臣慷慨誓諸將曰：「今日之事，係國安危，勝則富貴可保，敗則身戮家亡。

translations.literal: Suddenly a great force arrived at Yaobigu; the two armies faced each other. Liangchen, impassioned, swore to the generals, "Today's affair concerns the state's safety and peril—if we win, wealth and honor can be preserved; if we lose, bodies will be slaughtered and families destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels massed at Yaobigu, Liangchen addressed his officers: "Today the realm's safety hangs in the balance—victory means wealth and honor; defeat means death for us and ruin for our families.

sentences.zh: 苟能用命，縱死行間，不失忠孝之名。」

translations.literal: If you can exert your lives, though you die on the march you will not lose the name of loyalty and filial piety."
translations.idiomatic: If you give your all, even death on the field will leave your loyalty untarnished."

sentences.zh: 衆聞，踴躍而前。

translations.literal: When the masses heard, they leaped forward.
translations.idiomatic: The men leaped to the attack.

sentences.zh: 會大風揚沙，晝晦，良臣手刃數十人，賊勢沮，衆軍乘勝擣之，賊大潰，獲阿藍台兒、渾都海，殺之，西鄙輯寧。

translations.literal: A great wind arose and sand flew; day was dim. Liangchen with his own hand slew several tens of men; the rebels' momentum was checked; the mass of troops followed victory to storm them; the rebels were greatly routed; Alantai'er and Hunduhai were captured and killed; the western border was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: A sandstorm darkened the day; Liangchen himself cut down dozens of men, the rebel line wavered, and his troops routed them, capturing and killing Alantai'er and Hunduhai and pacifying the west.

sentences.zh: 捷聞，賜金虎符，權便宜都緫帥。

translations.literal: When victory was reported, he was granted a gold tiger tally and authorized as Regional Commander with discretionary powers.
translations.idiomatic: News of victory brought him a gold tiger tally and authority as regional commander.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，火里叛，復討平之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong, Huoli rebelled; he again campaigned and pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongtong (1261), Huoli rebelled; Liangchen put down the revolt again.

sentences.zh: 入覲，賜燕，屢稱其功，良臣拜謝曰：「臣奉諸王成筭，何功之有！」

translations.literal: He had audience; a banquet was granted; his achievements were repeatedly praised. Liangchen bowed in thanks and said, "Your servant carried out the princes' plans—what achievement was there!"
translations.idiomatic: At court he was feasted and praised; Liangchen demurred, "I only carried out the princes' strategy—what merit is mine?"

sentences.zh: 世祖嘉其能讓，復賜金鞍、甲冑、弓矢，轉同僉鞏昌路便宜都緫帥。

translations.literal: Shizu commended his ability to yield; he was again granted a gold saddle, armor, and bow and arrows, and transferred to co-signatory Regional Commander of the Gongchang Circuit with discretionary powers.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai admired his modesty, gave him a gold saddle, armor, and bow, and made him co-commander of Gongchang.

sentences.zh: 宋將昝萬壽帥戰船二百，泝江而上，欲掩青居。

translations.literal: Song general Zan Wanshou commanded two hundred warships and went upriver, intending to seize Qingju.
translations.idiomatic: The Song general Zan Wanshou led two hundred warships upriver to strike Qingju.

sentences.zh: 良臣伏甲數十艘其後，身先逆戰，萬壽敗走，伏發，幾獲之。

translations.literal: Liangchen hid armor on several tens of boats in his rear; he himself led the counterattack in the van; Wanshou was defeated and fled; the ambush was sprung and he was nearly captured.
translations.idiomatic: Liangchen hid armed boats behind him, led the counterattack in person, routed Wanshou, and nearly took him when the ambush closed.

sentences.zh: 三年，授閬蓬廣安順慶等路征南都元帥。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Grand Marshal of the Southern Campaign for Lang, Peng, Guang'an, Shunqing, and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was made grand marshal of the southern campaign over Lang, Peng, Guang'an, Shunqing, and related circuits.

sentences.zh: 良臣以釣魚山險絕，不可攻，奏請就近地築城曰武勝，以扼其往來。

translations.literal: Liangchen, because Diaoyushan was perilous and sheer and could not be attacked, memorialized asking to build a city at a nearby place called Wusheng to choke their comings and goings.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Diaoyu Fortress impregnable, he asked to build a new fortress called Wusheng nearby to block Song movements.

sentences.zh: 四年春，良臣攻重慶，命元帥康土禿先驅，與宋將朱禩孫兵交，良臣塞其歸路，引兵橫擊之，斷敵兵為二，敵敗走趨城，不得入，盡殺之。

translations.literal: In spring of the fourth year Liangchen attacked Chongqing, ordering Marshal Kang Tuhu as vanguard; he engaged Song general Zhu Qisun's troops; Liangchen blocked their return route and led troops to strike across, cutting the enemy army in two; the enemy fled toward the city, could not enter, and were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth spring he attacked Chongqing; his vanguard Kang Tuhu fought Zhu Qisun; Liangchen cut the retreat, split the Song force in two, and slaughtered those who could not re-enter the city.

sentences.zh: 至元六年，授東川副統軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan he was appointed Deputy Commander-in-Chief of Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Zhiyuan (1269) he was made deputy commander-in-chief of Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 八年，兄子惟正請於朝，謂良臣久勞戎行，乞身代之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year his nephew Weizheng petitioned the court, saying Liangchen had long labored on campaign and begging to replace him in person.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year his nephew Weizheng asked the court to relieve him after long service on campaign.

sentences.zh: 九年，復授良臣昭勇大將軍、鞏昌等二十四處便宜都緫帥，兼本路諸軍奧魯緫管。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Liangchen was again appointed Valiant-and-Resolute Grand General and Regional Commander with discretionary powers over twenty-four posts including Gongchang, and concurrently Grand Administrator of all örüg forces of this circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was reappointed valiant-and-resolute grand general and regional commander over twenty-four circuits including Gongchang, with command of local örüg forces.

sentences.zh: 明年，召入，帝曰：「成都被兵久，須卿安集之。」

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned in; the emperor said, "Chengdu has long suffered from troops—you are needed to settle it."
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was summoned; the emperor said, "Chengdu has suffered war too long—you must restore order there."

sentences.zh: 授鎮國上將軍、樞密副使、西川行樞密院事，蜀人安之。

translations.literal: He was appointed Pacifying-the-Realm General, Vice Minister of the Secretariat for Military Affairs, and Commissioner of the Western Sichuan Branch Secretariat for Military Affairs; the people of Shu were settled.
translations.idiomatic: He was made pacifying-the-realm general, vice minister of military affairs, and head of the western Sichuan secretariat; the Shu people were reassured.

sentences.zh: 十一年，進攻嘉定，昝萬壽堅守不出，良臣度有伏兵，大搜山谷，果得而殺之，進壘薄城。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he advanced to attack Jiading; Zan Wanshou held firm and would not come out; Liangchen judged there were ambush troops, searched the mountains and valleys on a large scale, indeed found and killed them, and advanced to camp pressing the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he besieged Jiading; Zan Wanshou held the walls; Liangchen scoured the hills for ambushes, killed them, and pressed the siege.

sentences.zh: 萬壽悉軍出戰，大破之，伏尸蔽江，萬壽乞降，良臣奏免其死，居民按堵。

translations.literal: Wanshou led all his troops out to fight and was greatly defeated; corpses covered the river; Wanshou begged to surrender; Liangchen memorialized to spare his life; the residents were undisturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Wanshou sallied with his whole force, was crushed, and corpses choked the river; he begged to surrender; Liangchen spared him, and the people were left in peace.

sentences.zh: 良臣統兵順流而下。

translations.literal: Liangchen commanded troops downstream along the current.
translations.idiomatic: Liangchen led his army downriver.

sentences.zh: 紫雲、瀘、敘相繼款附。

translations.literal: Ziyun, Lu, and Xu submitted in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyun, Luzhou, and Xuzhou surrendered in turn.

sentences.zh: 還圍重慶。

translations.literal: He returned to besiege Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to invest Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 十三年，宋涪州安撫楊立，帥兵救重慶者再，良臣皆敗走之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Song Fuzhou pacification commissioner Yang Li twice led troops to relieve Chongqing; Liangchen defeated and drove him off both times.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the Song pacification commissioner Yang Li of Fuzhou twice tried to relieve Chongqing; Liangchen beat him back each time.

sentences.zh: 宋安撫張珏，遣將乘虛襲據瀘州，良臣還軍平之。

translations.literal: Song pacification commissioner Zhang Jue sent a general to seize Luzhou by surprise while it was empty; Liangchen returned his army and pacified it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jue sent a raiding force to seize Luzhou; Liangchen turned back and recovered it.

sentences.zh: 復攻重慶。

translations.literal: He again attacked Chongqing.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Chongqing again.

sentences.zh: 十五年春，張珏悉衆鏖戰，良臣奮擊，大破之，身中四矢。

translations.literal: In spring of the fifteenth year Zhang Jue led all his forces in fierce battle; Liangchen struck vigorously and routed them greatly; he was wounded by four arrows.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth spring Zhang Jue fought all out; Liangchen broke him but took four arrows.

sentences.zh: 明日，督戰益急。

translations.literal: The next day he pressed the battle still more urgently.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he pressed the assault harder still.

sentences.zh: 珏所部趙安開門納降，珏潛遁。

translations.literal: Jue's subordinate Zhao An opened the gate to receive surrender; Jue slipped away in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao An opened the gates; Zhang Jue fled in secret.

sentences.zh: 良臣禁俘掠，發粟賑饑，民大悅。

translations.literal: Liangchen forbade plundering captives, issued grain to relieve famine; the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Liangchen forbade looting, distributed grain to the hungry, and won the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 四川悉平，捷聞，世祖喜甚，召良臣入覲，授資善大夫、中書左丞、行四川中書省事，賜白貂裘。

translations.literal: When Sichuan was entirely pacified and victory was reported, Shizu was exceedingly pleased and summoned Liangchen to audience, appointing him Worthy-and-Kind Grand Master, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Commissioner of the Sichuan Branch of the Central Secretariat, and granting a white sable coat.
translations.idiomatic: When Sichuan was fully pacified, Kublai rejoiced, summoned Liangchen, made him worthy-and-kind grand master and left vice director of the Sichuan secretariat, and gave him a white sable coat.

sentences.zh: 良臣陳治蜀十五事，世祖喜納。

translations.literal: Liangchen presented fifteen items on governing Shu; Shizu gladly accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: Liangchen submitted fifteen proposals for governing Shu, all of which Kublai approved.

sentences.zh: 良臣至成都，以蜀瘡痍之餘，極意循撫。

translations.literal: Liangchen reached Chengdu and, because Shu was in the aftermath of wounds, exerted his utmost in soothing governance.
translations.idiomatic: At Chengdu he devoted himself to healing a land ravaged by war.

sentences.zh: 行省罷。

translations.literal: The branch secretariat was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The branch secretariat was then abolished.

sentences.zh: 改授安西王相，不赴。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as counselor to the Prince of Anxi but did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He was named counselor to the Prince of Anxi but declined to take up the post.

sentences.zh: 十八年夏，疾卒。

translations.literal: In summer of the eighteenth year he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the eighteenth year he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 年五十一。

translations.literal: He was fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 贈儀同三司，諡忠惠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted the rank of Minister of State with Threefold Parity and given the posthumous name Zhonghui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given minister-of-state rank and the temple name Zhonghui (Loyal and Kind).

sentences.zh: 加贈推誠保德宣力功臣、儀同三司、陝西等處行中書省平章政事、柱國，追封梁國公。

translations.literal: Further posthumous honors were added: Faithful-and-Trustworthy Merit-Exerting Minister Supporting Virtue, Minister of State with Threefold Parity, Pacification Commissioner of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, Pillar of the State, and he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He was further honored as faithful merit minister, pacification commissioner of Shaanxi, pillar of the state, and posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Liang.

sentences.zh: 子七人：惟勤，雲南諸路行省平章政事；

translations.literal: He had seven sons: Weiqin, Pacification Commissioner of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons: Weiqin, pacification commissioner of Yunnan;

sentences.zh: 惟簡，保寧萬戶；

translations.literal: Weijian, commander of ten thousand households of Baoning;
translations.idiomatic: Weijian, commander of the Baoning ten-thousand-household unit;

sentences.zh: 惟某，同知屯田緫管府事；

translations.literal: Wei [name unknown], Associate Administrator of the Garrison-Farming Directorate;
translations.idiomatic: one son [name lost in text], associate administrator of the garrison-farming directorate;

sentences.zh: 惟永，征西都元帥；

translations.literal: Weiyong, Grand Marshal of the Western Campaign;
translations.idiomatic: Weiyong, grand marshal of the western campaign;

sentences.zh: 惟恭，階州同知；

translations.literal: Weigong, Associate Prefect of Jiezhou;
translations.idiomatic: Weigong, associate prefect of Jiezhou;

sentences.zh: 惟仁，人匠緫管達魯花赤；

translations.literal: Weiren, darughachi of the Artisans Directorate;
translations.idiomatic: Weiren, darughachi of the artisans directorate;

sentences.zh: 惟新，漢軍千戶。

translations.literal: Weixin, commander of a thousand households of Han troops.
translations.idiomatic: and Weixin, commander of a Han thousand-household unit.

sentences.zh: 惟正字公理，幼穎悟，藏書二萬卷，喜從文士論議古今治亂，尤喜談兵，時出游獵，則勒從騎為攻守狀。

translations.literal: Weizheng, courtesy name Gongli, was clever from childhood; he had twenty thousand volumes in his library; he delighted in discussing with literary men the rise and fall of past and present and the ordering of chaos, and especially delighted in discussing warfare; when he went out hunting he would array his mounted followers in attack-and-defense formations.
translations.idiomatic: Weizheng, courtesy name Gongli, was precocious, kept twenty thousand books, loved to debate history and strategy with scholars, and on hunts drilled his escort in mock battle formations.

sentences.zh: 父卒于軍，皇姪壽王俾權襲父爵，守青居山。

translations.literal: When his father died in the army, the imperial nephew Prince Shou ordered him to act in inheriting his father's title and guard Qingju Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died on campaign, Prince Shou had him act in his father's place guarding Mount Qingju.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，遂真授焉。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, he was truly appointed.
translations.idiomatic: When Kublai came to the throne, the appointment was confirmed.

sentences.zh: 初，憲宗遣渾都海以騎兵二萬守六盤，又遣乞台不花守青居，至是，渾都海叛，乞台不花發兵為應，惟正即命力士縛乞台不花，殺之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Emperor Xianzong had sent Hunduhai with twenty thousand cavalry to guard Liupan and also sent Qitai Buhua to guard Qingju; by this time Hunduhai had rebelled and Qitai Buhua raised troops in response; Weizheng immediately ordered strong men to bind Qitai Buhua and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Möngke had posted Hunduhai with twenty thousand horse at Liupan and Qitai Buhua at Qingju; when Hunduhai rebelled and Qitai Buhua rose in support, Weizheng had him seized and executed.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘉其功，詔東川軍事悉聽處分。

translations.literal: Shizu commended his achievement and ordered that all Dongchuan military affairs heed his disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai praised him and placed all Dongchuan military affairs under his command.

sentences.zh: 中統二年，入朝，賜甲冑、寶鞍。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongtong he came to court and was granted armor and a precious saddle.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongtong he attended court and received armor and a fine saddle.

sentences.zh: 三年，詔還鞏昌。

translations.literal: In the third year he was ordered back to Gongchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was ordered back to Gongchang.

sentences.zh: 部長火都叛，民大擾，惟正謂將吏曰：「火都今若猘犬，方肆狂齧，苟一戰不利，則城邑為墟，當勝以不戰。」

translations.literal: The tribal chief Huodu rebelled and the people were greatly disturbed. Weizheng said to his officers and clerks, "Huodu is now like a mad dog wildly biting; if one battle goes badly the cities and towns will be ruins—we should conquer him without fighting."
translations.idiomatic: When the tribal chief Huodu rebelled, Weizheng told his staff, "Huodu is a mad dog—one lost battle would ruin the region; we must beat him without a pitched battle."

sentences.zh: 乃發兵踵之，賊欲戰不得，休則撓之，若是者兩月，知其糧盡勢蹙，曰：「可矣。」

translations.literal: He then sent troops to follow on his heels; the rebels wished to fight but could not; when they rested he harassed them; thus for two months, knowing their grain was exhausted and their momentum pressed, he said, "It can be done."
translations.idiomatic: He harried them for two months until their grain ran out, then said, "Now."

sentences.zh: 與戰，屢捷，火都遣三十人來約降，即遣其十人還，俾火都自來，因潛兵躡其後，出其不意擒殺之。

translations.literal: He fought them and repeatedly won; Huodu sent thirty men to arrange surrender; he sent ten of them back, ordering Huodu to come in person, while secretly sending troops to follow behind, and by surprise captured and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated victories Huodu sent thirty men to negotiate; Weizheng sent ten back demanding Huodu come in person, then ambushed and killed him.

sentences.zh: 至元七年，宋人修合州，詔立武勝軍以拒之。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan the Song repaired Hezhou; an edict ordered the Wusheng Army established to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Zhiyuan (1270), when the Song repaired Hezhou, the court established the Wusheng army to block them.

sentences.zh: 惟正臨嘉陵江作柵，阨其水道，夜懸燈柵間，編竹為籠，中置火炬，順地勢轉走，照百步外，以防不虞，宋人知有備，不敢近。

translations.literal: Weizheng built stockades along the Jialing River to choke their water route; at night he hung lamps between the stockades, weaving bamboo into cages with torches inside that turned with the terrain, illuminating a hundred paces beyond to guard against the unexpected; the Song knew there were preparations and did not dare approach.
translations.idiomatic: Weizheng built palisades on the Jialing to block the waterway and lit bamboo torch cages that rotated with the terrain, lighting a hundred paces around so the Song dared not approach.

sentences.zh: 九年，帥兵掠忠、涪，獲令、簿各一，破寨七，擒守將六，降戶千六百有奇，捕虜五百。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he led troops to raid Zhong and Fu, obtaining one magistrate's register and one clerk's register each, breaking seven stockades, capturing six defending generals, reducing more than sixteen hundred households, and taking five hundred captives.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he raided Zhong and Fu, took local registers, stormed seven forts, captured six commanders, received the submission of more than 1,600 households, and took five hundred prisoners.

sentences.zh: 會丞相伯顏克襄陽，議取宋，惟正奏曰：「蜀未下者，數城耳，宜併力攻餘杭，本根既拔，此將焉往！

translations.literal: When Chancellor Bayan took Xiangyang and they discussed taking the Song, Weizheng memorialized, "Of Shu what is not yet taken is only a few cities; it is fitting to concentrate force to attack Yuhang—once the root is pulled up, where can these go!
translations.idiomatic: When Bayan took Xiangyang and the court debated conquering the Song, Weizheng argued, "Only a few Shu strongholds remain—we should strike Hangzhou; cut the root and the branches will wither!

sentences.zh: 願以本兵，由嘉陵下夔峽，與伯顏會錢塘。」

translations.literal: I wish to lead my native troops down the Jialing through Kuixia to meet Bayan at Qiantang."
translations.idiomatic: Let me lead my troops down the Jialing through the Kuixia Gorge to join Bayan at Qiantang."

sentences.zh: 帝優詔荅曰：「四川事重，舍卿誰託！

translations.literal: The emperor with a gracious edict replied, "Sichuan affairs are weighty—apart from you, to whom can they be entrusted!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied graciously, "Sichuan is too important to leave to anyone else!

sentences.zh: 異日蜀平，功豈伯顏下邪！」

translations.literal: When Shu is pacified another day, will the achievement be beneath Bayan's!"
translations.idiomatic: When Shu is pacified, your merit will not rank below Bayan's!"

sentences.zh: 未幾，兩川樞密院合兵圍重慶，命益兵助之，惟正奪其洪崖門，獲宋將何統制。

translations.literal: Before long the two Sichuan branch secretariats for military affairs combined forces to besiege Chongqing; troops were ordered increased to assist; Weizheng seized their Hongya Gate and captured Song commander He Tongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the two Sichuan military secretariats besieged Chongqing; Weizheng stormed the Hongya Gate and captured the Song commander He.

sentences.zh: 皇子安西王出鎮秦蜀，召惟正還。

translations.literal: The Prince of Anxi went out to guard Qin and Shu and summoned Weizheng back.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Anxi took charge of Qin and Shu, Weizheng was recalled.

sentences.zh: 十四年冬，皇子北伐，而藩王土魯叛於六盤，王相府命別速帶領兵進討，惟正為副。

translations.literal: In winter of the fourteenth year the prince campaigned north while the frontier prince Tulu rebelled at Liupan; the prince's council ordered Biesudai to lead troops forward to suppress; Weizheng was deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth winter, while the prince campaigned north, the frontier prince Tulu rebelled at Liupan; Biesudai was sent to suppress him with Weizheng as deputy.

sentences.zh: 別速帶不習兵，師行無紀，惟正為正部曲，肅行陣，嚴斥候，凡軍政一倚重焉。

translations.literal: Biesudai was unskilled in warfare; the army marched without discipline; Weizheng for the main body of troops enforced battle order, strict scouts—for all military government he was wholly relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Biesudai knew little of war and marched without discipline; Weizheng imposed order, strict scouting, and bore the real military burden.

sentences.zh: 進次平涼，簡鞏兵銳者八十人與俱，至六盤。

translations.literal: Advancing to Pingliang, he selected eighty sharp Gong troops to accompany him to Liupan.
translations.idiomatic: At Pingliang he took eighty picked Gongchang troops on to Liupan.

sentences.zh: 土魯先據西山，惟正分安西兵為左右翼，鞏兵獨居中，去土魯一里許，皆下馬，手弓。

translations.literal: Tulu had first occupied West Mountain; Weizheng divided the Anxi troops into left and right wings, with Gong troops alone in the center; one li from Tulu all dismounted with hand bows.
translations.idiomatic: Tulu held West Mountain; Weizheng split the Anxi force on both wings, placed Gong troops in the center, and a li from the enemy ordered all to dismount with bows in hand.

sentences.zh: 土魯遣百騎突陳，惟正令引滿毋發，將及。

translations.literal: Tulu sent a hundred horsemen to charge the line; Weizheng ordered them to draw to the full but not release; they were nearly upon them.
translations.idiomatic: Tulu sent a hundred horsemen to charge; Weizheng ordered full draws but held fire until they were almost upon them.

sentences.zh: 又命曰：「視必中而發。」

translations.literal: He again ordered, "Look for certain hits before releasing."
translations.idiomatic: He ordered, "Shoot only when you are sure to hit."

sentences.zh: 於是矢下如雨，突騎中者三之一，餘盡馳還，土魯軍遂走。

translations.literal: Thereupon arrows fell like rain; of the charging horsemen one in three was hit; the rest all galloped back; Tulu's army then fled.
translations.idiomatic: Arrows fell like rain; a third of the chargers fell; the rest fled and Tulu's army broke.

sentences.zh: 惟正麾兵逐之，三踰山，至蕭河，擒叛將燕只哥，復進兵，土魯亦就擒。

translations.literal: Weizheng commanded troops in pursuit, crossed three mountains to Xiaohe, captured the rebel general Yanzhi'ge, advanced again, and Tulu was also captured.
translations.idiomatic: Weizheng pursued over three mountains to the Xiao River, captured the rebel general Yanzhi'ge, and then took Tulu himself.

sentences.zh: 安西王至，惟正迎謁，王歷稱其功。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Anxi arrived, Weizheng went to meet him in audience; the prince repeatedly praised his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Anxi arrived, Weizheng met him and was repeatedly praised.

sentences.zh: 明日，大燕，賞以金尊杯、貂裘。

translations.literal: The next day a great banquet was held; he was rewarded with a gold goblet and sable coat.
translations.idiomatic: The next day at a great banquet he received a gold cup and sable coat.

sentences.zh: 王妃賜其母珠絡帽衣，且曰：「吾皇家兒婦也，為汝母製衣，汝母真福人也。」

translations.literal: The princess bestowed on his mother a pearl-net cap and robe and said, "I am a daughter-in-law of the imperial house; I made clothes for your mother—your mother is truly a fortunate person."
translations.idiomatic: The princess gave his mother a pearl-trimmed hat and robe, saying, "As a daughter of the imperial house I made this for your mother—a fortunate woman indeed."

sentences.zh: 詔惟正入朝，世祖推玉食食之，賜白金五千兩、錦衣一襲，授金吾衛上將軍、開成路宣慰使。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Weizheng to come to court; Shizu pushed imperial food for him to eat, granted five thousand taels of white gold and one suit of brocade robes, and appointed him General of the Golden Spear Guard and Pacification Commissioner of Kaicheng Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to court, Kublai fed him from the imperial table, gave five thousand taels of silver and brocade robes, and made him general of the Golden Spear Guard and pacification commissioner of Kaicheng.

sentences.zh: 十七年，遷龍虎衛上將軍、中書左丞，行秦蜀中書省事，賜玉帶。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was transferred to General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Commissioner of the Qin-Shu Branch of the Central Secretariat, and granted a jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he became general of the Dragon-Tiger Guard, left vice director of the secretariat, and commissioner of the Qin-Shu branch, with a jade belt.

sentences.zh: 以省治在長安，去蜀遠，乃命惟正分省于蜀。

translations.literal: Because the secretariat was at Chang'an, far from Shu, Weizheng was ordered to branch the secretariat in Shu.
translations.idiomatic: As the secretariat sat in Chang'an, far from Shu, he was given a separate Shu office.

sentences.zh: 蜀土荐罹兵革，民無完居，一聞馬嘶，輒奔竄避匿，惟正留意撫循，人便安之。

translations.literal: Shu soil had repeatedly suffered from troops and arms; the people had no intact dwellings; at the sound of horses they would flee and hide; Weizheng took care to soothe and comfort, and people found it convenient and were settled.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had been ravaged by war; at the sound of hooves people fled; Weizheng soothed them until they no longer lived in fear.

sentences.zh: 二十年，進階資德大夫。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was advanced in rank to Worthy-and-Virtuous Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was promoted to worthy-and-virtuous grand master.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，改授陝西行中書省左丞。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was reassigned as Left Vice Director of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was made left vice director of the Shaanxi secretariat.

sentences.zh: 入覲上都，得腹疾，還至華州，卒，年四十四。

translations.literal: He had audience at Shangdu, contracted a belly illness, returned to Huazhou, and died; he was forty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He attended court at Shangdu, fell ill, returned to Huazhou, and died at forty-four.

sentences.zh: 諡貞肅。

translations.literal: His posthumous name was Zhensu.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Zhensu (Steadfast and Solemn).

sentences.zh: 二子：嗣昌，武略將軍、成都管軍副萬戶；

translations.literal: Two sons: Sichang, Martial-Strategy General and Deputy Commander of Ten Thousand Households of the Chengdu Garrison;
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Sichang, martial-strategy general and deputy commander of the Chengdu garrison;

sentences.zh: 壽昌，資德大夫、江南行御史臺中丞。

translations.literal: Shouchang, Worthy-and-Virtuous Grand Master and Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: and Shouchang, worthy-and-virtuous grand master and vice censor-in-chief of the Jiangnan censorate.

sentences.zh: 史天澤格

translations.literal: Shi Tianze [biography follows]
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tianze

sentences.zh: 史天澤字潤甫，秉直季子也。

translations.literal: Shi Tianze, courtesy name Runfu, was the youngest son of Bingzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Tianze, whose courtesy name was Runfu, was the youngest son of Bingzhi.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，音如洪鍾，善騎射，勇力絕人，從其兄天倪帥真定。

translations.literal: He stood eight feet tall, his voice like a great bell; he excelled at riding and archery, and his courage and strength were unmatched among men; he followed his elder brother Tianni in commanding Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: He stood eight feet tall, spoke like a great bell, excelled at riding and archery, and possessed matchless strength; he followed his elder brother Tianni in governing Zhending.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，天倪遣護送其母歸北京，既而天倪為武仙所害，府僚王縉、王守道追及天澤於燕，曰：「變起倉猝，部曲散走，多在近郊，公能迴轡南行，不招自至矣。」

translations.literal: In the yiyou year Tianni sent escorts to return their mother to the Northern Capital; before long Tianni was killed by Wu Xian; prefectural staff Wang Jin and Wang Shoudao caught up with Tianze in Yan and said, "The change arose in sudden haste and the troops scattered; most are in the nearby suburbs—if you can turn your reins south, they will come without being summoned."
translations.idiomatic: In yiyou, Tianni sent their mother north; soon Wu Xian murdered him. Officials Wang Jin and Wang Shoudao overtook Tianze in Yan and urged him, "The crisis was sudden and the troops have scattered nearby—turn south and they will rally to you without a summons."

sentences.zh: 天澤毅然曰：「兄弟之讎，義所當復，雖死不避，況未必死邪！」

translations.literal: Tianze said resolutely, "A brother's vengeance is what righteousness demands; though one die one does not avoid it—besides, one may not necessarily die!"
translations.idiomatic: Tianze answered firmly, "Blood vengeance is my duty; I will not shrink from it even at the risk of death—and I may not die at all!"

sentences.zh: 即傾貲裝，易甲仗，南還，行次滿城，得士馬甚衆。

translations.literal: He immediately poured out his goods and baggage, exchanged armor and weapons, and returned south; halting at Mancheng he gathered a great host of men and horses.
translations.idiomatic: He spent his fortune on arms and rode south; at Mancheng he gathered a large force.

sentences.zh: 天澤攝行軍事，遣監軍李伯祐詣國王孛魯言狀，且乞濟師。

translations.literal: Tianze acted in military affairs and sent supervising officer Li Boyou to Prince Bolu to report the situation and beg for relief troops.
translations.idiomatic: Acting commander, he sent Li Boyou to Prince Bolu to report events and request reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 天澤時為帳前軍緫領，孛魯承制命紹兄職為都元帥。

translations.literal: At the time Tianze was chief of the vanguard guard; Bolu by commission appointed him to succeed his brother's post as Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Tianze was then chief of the imperial guard; Bolu confirmed him as grand marshal in his brother's place.

sentences.zh: 俾笑乃將蒙古軍三千人援之，合勢進攻盧奴。

translations.literal: He ordered Xiaonai to lead three thousand Mongol troops to aid him; combining forces they advanced to attack Lunu.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaonai brought three thousand Mongol horsemen; together they assaulted Lunu.

sentences.zh: 仙驍將葛鐵槍者，擁衆萬人來拒戰，天澤迎擊之，身先士卒，勇氣百倍。

translations.literal: Xian's fierce general Ge Tieqiang led ten thousand men to resist; Tianze met them in battle, himself taking the lead, his courage a hundredfold.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian's champion Ge Tieqiang blocked him with ten thousand men; Tianze led the charge himself, fighting with redoubled fury.

sentences.zh: 賊退阻泒河，乘夜而遁，天澤追及之，生擒葛鐵槍，餘衆悉潰，獲其兵甲輜重，軍威大振。

translations.literal: The rebels retreated and were blocked by the Zhuo River; they fled by night; Tianze overtook them, captured Ge Tieqiang alive, and the rest all scattered; they seized armor, weapons, and baggage; military prestige greatly rose.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy fled toward the Zhuo River by night; Tianze overtook them, captured Ge Tieqiang alive, and routed the rest, seizing arms and wagons and greatly raising his army's renown.

sentences.zh: 遂下中山，略無極，拔趙州，進軍野頭。

translations.literal: He then took Zhongshan, overran Wuji, seized Zhaozhou, and advanced to Yetou.
translations.idiomatic: He took Zhongshan, overran Wuji, captured Zhaozhou, and advanced to Yetou.

sentences.zh: 會天澤兄天安亦提兵來赴，擊仙敗之，仙奔雙門，遂復真定。

translations.literal: Tianze's elder brother Tian'an also led troops to join; they defeated Xian; Xian fled to Shuangmen; Zhending was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Tian'an arrived with reinforcements; they beat Wu Xian, who fled to Shuangmen, and recovered Zhending.

sentences.zh: 未幾，宋大名緫管彭義斌陰與仙合，欲取真定，天澤同笑乃扼諸贊皇，仙不得進。

translations.literal: Before long Song Grand Coordinator of Daming Peng Yibin secretly joined with Xian to take Zhending; Tianze with Xiaonai blocked the passes at Zanhuang and Xian could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Song coordinator Peng Yibin allied secretly with Wu Xian to seize Zhending; Tianze and Xiaonai held Zanhuang Pass and blocked them.

sentences.zh: 義斌勢蹙，焚山自守，天澤遣銳卒五十，摧鋒而入，自以鐵騎繼其後，縛義斌斬之。

translations.literal: Yibin was pressed; he burned the mountains and held in defense; Tianze sent fifty elite troops to break the line and enter; he himself followed with iron cavalry, bound Yibin, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Yibin burned the hills and held out; Tianze sent fifty shock troops through the line, followed with cavalry, captured Peng Yibin, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，仙復令諜者，結死士於城中大曆寺為內應，夜斬關而入，據其城。

translations.literal: Before long Xian again sent agents to rally die-hards in the city at the Dali Temple as inside collaborators; by night they cut the gate bar and entered, seizing the city.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian soon planted agents in the Dali Temple to open the gates by night and seized the city.

sentences.zh: 天澤引步卒數十，踰城東出，至藁城，求援於董俊。

translations.literal: Tianze led several tens of foot soldiers, climbed over the east wall and went out, reached Gaocheng, and sought aid from Dong Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Tianze slipped out over the east wall with a handful of infantry, reached Gaocheng, and sought help from Dong Jun.

sentences.zh: 俊授以銳卒數百，夜赴真定，而笑乃兵亦至，捕叛者三百餘人，仙從數騎，走保西山抱犢寨。

translations.literal: Jun gave him several hundred sharp troops; they went to Zhending by night while Xiaonai's troops also arrived; more than three hundred rebels were captured; Xian with a few horsemen fled to hold the Baodu stockade in the Western Hills.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jun gave him picked troops; by night they reached Zhending as Xiaonai arrived, seized three hundred rebels, and Wu Xian fled with a few riders to the Baodu stockade.

sentences.zh: 笑乃怒忿民之從賊，驅萬餘人將殺之，天澤曰：「彼皆吾民，但為賊所脅耳，殺之何罪！」

translations.literal: Xiaonai angrily wished to kill more than ten thousand people who had followed the rebels, saying they were all his people but had been coerced by bandits—what crime in killing them!
translations.idiomatic: Xiaonai meant to massacre ten thousand townspeople who had sided with the rebels; Tianze protested, "They are our people, forced by the enemy—what crime is theirs?"

sentences.zh: 力爭得釋。

translations.literal: By strenuous argument they were released.
translations.idiomatic: He argued until they were spared.

sentences.zh: 乃繕城壁，立樓櫓，為不可犯之計，招集流散，存恤困窮。

translations.literal: He then repaired walls and towers, set up watchtowers as a plan none could violate, gathered the scattered, and comforted the distressed.
translations.idiomatic: He rebuilt walls and watchtowers, recalled refugees, and relieved the destitute.

sentences.zh: 以抱犢諸寨，仙之巢穴，不即剪覆，終遺後患，急攻下之，仙乃遁去。

translations.literal: Because the Baodu stockades were Xian's nest and were not immediately destroyed, leaving later trouble, he urgently attacked and took them; Xian then fled away.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed the Baodu strongholds, Wu Xian's last refuge, and drove him off for good.

sentences.zh: 繼又取蟻尖、馬武等寨，而相、衛亦降。

translations.literal: He next took Yijian, Mawu, and other stockades; Xiang and Wei also submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He took Yijian, Mawu, and other forts; Xiangzhou and Weizhou surrendered.

sentences.zh: 壬辰春，太宗由白坡渡河，詔天澤以兵由孟津會河南，至則睿宗已破合達軍于三峰山。

translations.literal: In spring of the renchen year Emperor Taizong crossed from Baipo; he ordered Tianze to lead troops from Mengjin to join Henan; when he arrived Prince Ruizong had already broken Heda's army at Sanfengshan.
translations.idiomatic: In renchen spring Taizong crossed at Baipo and ordered Tianze to join the Henan front via Mengjin; by the time he arrived, Prince Tolui had already crushed Heda at Sanfengshan.

sentences.zh: 乃命略地京東，招降太康、柘縣、瓦岡、睢州，追斬金將完顏慶山奴於陽邑。

translations.literal: He was ordered to overrun the eastern capital region, receiving the surrender of Taikang, Zhe, Wagang, and Suizhou, and pursued and beheaded Jin general Wanyan Qingshan'nu at Yangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He overran eastern Henan, received Taikang, Zhe, Wagang, and Suizhou, and killed the Jin general Wanyan Qingshan'nu at Yangyi.

sentences.zh: 夏，帝北還，留睿宗緫兵圍汴。

translations.literal: In summer the emperor returned north, leaving Prince Ruizong to command the army besieging Bian.
translations.idiomatic: That summer the emperor went north, leaving Tolui to besiege Bianliang.

sentences.zh: 癸巳春，金主突圍而出，令完顏白撒自黃龍岡來襲新衛。

translations.literal: In spring of the guisi year the Jin ruler broke out; he ordered Wanyan Baisha from Huanglonggang to strike Xinwei.
translations.idiomatic: In guisi spring the Jin emperor broke out of the siege; Wanyan Baisha was sent from Huanglonggang against Xinwei.

sentences.zh: 天澤率輕騎馳赴之，比至，圍已合，天澤奮戈突至城下，呼守者曰：「汝等勉力，援兵且至。」

translations.literal: Tianze led light cavalry in a rush; when he arrived the siege was already closed; Tianze brandished his spear and dashed to beneath the walls, calling to the defenders, "You must strive—relief is coming."
translations.idiomatic: Tianze galloped ahead; finding the encirclement complete, he fought to the walls and shouted, "Hold fast—help is near!"

sentences.zh: 復躍出，其衆皆披靡，遂與大軍夾擊之，白撒等敗走蒲城，天澤尾其後，白撒等兵尚八萬，俘斬殆盡。

translations.literal: He leaped out again; the masses all scattered; he joined the great army in a pincer; Baisha and others fled to Pucheng; Tianze followed; Baisha and others still had eighty thousand troops; captives and heads were nearly all taken.
translations.idiomatic: He broke out, rallied the main force, and crushed Baisha at Pucheng; of his eighty thousand men nearly all were killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 金主以單舸東走歸德，天澤追至歸德，與諸軍會。

translations.literal: The Jin ruler fled east in a single boat to Guide; Tianze pursued to Guide and joined the other armies.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin emperor fled by boat to Guide; Tianze pursued and joined the converging armies.

sentences.zh: 新衛達魯花赤撒吉思不花，欲薄城背水而營，天澤曰：「此豈駐兵之地乎！

translations.literal: The darughachi of Xinwei, Sagisibuhua, wished to camp close to the city with water at his back; Tianze said, "How is this a place to station troops!
translations.idiomatic: Sagisibuhua, darughachi of Xinwei, wanted to camp with his back to the water; Tianze warned, "That is no place to encamp!

sentences.zh: 彼若來犯，則進退失據矣。」

translations.literal: If they come to attack, advance and retreat will lose footing."
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy strikes, you will have no room to maneuver."

sentences.zh: 不聽，會天澤以事之汴，比還，撒吉思不花全軍皆沒。

translations.literal: He was not heeded; Tianze went to Bian on business; when he returned Sagisibuhua's whole army was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: His advice was ignored; when Tianze returned from an errand at Bian, Sagisibuhua's entire force had been wiped out.

sentences.zh: 金主遷蔡，帝命元帥盞率大軍圍之。

translations.literal: The Jin ruler moved to Cai; the emperor ordered the marshal to lead a great army to besiege it.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin court moved to Cai; the emperor ordered the field marshal to invest the city.

sentences.zh: 天澤當其北面，結筏潛渡汝水，血戰連日。

translations.literal: Tianze held the north face, built rafts to cross the Ru River in secret, and fought bloody battles for days on end.
translations.idiomatic: Tianze held the northern sector, rafted secretly across the Ru, and fought bloody battles day after day.

sentences.zh: 甲午春正月，蔡破，金主自經死，天澤還真定。

translations.literal: In spring of the first month of the jiawu year Cai fell; the Jin ruler hanged himself; Tianze returned to Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of jiawu, Cai fell; the Jin emperor hanged himself; Tianze returned to Zhending.

sentences.zh: 時政煩賦重，貸錢於西北賈人以代輸，累倍其息，謂之羊羔利，民不能給。

translations.literal: At the time government was troublesome and taxes heavy; they borrowed from northwestern merchants to pay substitutes, interest multiplying several times over—called "lamb-interest"—and the people could not repay.
translations.idiomatic: Taxes were crushing; people borrowed from Muslim merchants at usurious "lamb-interest" rates they could not repay.

sentences.zh: 天澤奏請官為償一本息而止。

translations.literal: Tianze memorialized asking the state to repay principal with interest once only.
translations.idiomatic: Tianze asked the state to redeem the debts for principal plus one year's interest only.

sentences.zh: 繼以歲饑，假貸充貢賦，積銀至一萬三千錠，天澤傾家貲，率族屬官吏代償之。

translations.literal: Later in years of famine they borrowed to meet tribute levies, silver accumulating to thirteen thousand ingots; Tianze spent his family fortune and led clan members and officials to repay on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: In famine years they borrowed again to pay taxes, amassing thirteen thousand ingots of silver; Tianze spent his family wealth and had kinsmen and officials repay it.

sentences.zh: 又請以中戶為軍，上下戶為民，著為定籍，境內以寧。

translations.literal: He also asked that middle households serve as soldiers and upper and lower households as civilians, fixing this as the registered norm; within the borders there was tranquility.
