translations.idiomatic: He fixed middle households as soldiers and upper and lower as civilians, stabilizing the registers and pacifying the region.

sentences.zh: 金亡，移軍伐宋。

translations.literal: When the Jin perished, he shifted the army to attack the Song.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jin fell, he turned to campaigns against the Song.

sentences.zh: 乙未，從皇子曲出攻棗陽，天澤先登，拔之。

translations.literal: In the yiwei year he followed Prince Quchu in attacking Zaoyang; Tianze was first to ascend and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In yiwei he followed Prince Quchu against Zaoyang and was first up the wall.

sentences.zh: 及攻襄陽，宋兵以舟數千陳於峭石灘，天澤挾二舟載死士，直前擣之，覆溺者萬計。

translations.literal: When they attacked Xiangyang, Song troops arrayed several thousand boats at Qiaoshi Beach; Tianze took two boats loaded with daredevils, went straight forward and stormed them; those overturned and drowned were counted in tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangyang the Song lined thousands of boats at Qiaoshi Beach; Tianze sent two suicide boats head-on and sank tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，從宗王口溫不花圍光州，天澤先破其外城，攻子城，又破之。

translations.literal: In the dingyou year he followed Prince Kouwenbuhua in besieging Guangzhou; Tianze first broke the outer city and attacked the inner city, breaking that too.
translations.idiomatic: In dingyou he followed Prince Kouwenbuhua at Guangzhou, stormed the outer and inner cities in succession.

sentences.zh: 師次復州，宋兵以舟三千鎖湖面為柵，天澤曰：「柵破，則復自潰。」

translations.literal: The army halted at Fuzhou; Song troops with three thousand boats chained the lake surface as a stockade; Tianze said, "When the stockade breaks, Fuzhou will collapse of itself."
translations.idiomatic: At Fuzhou the Song chained three thousand boats across the lake; Tianze said, "Break the boom and the city will fall."

sentences.zh: 親執桴鼓，督勇士四十人攻其柵，不踰時，柵破，復人懼，請降。

translations.literal: He personally took the oar and drum, directed forty brave men to attack the stockade; in less than an hour it was broken; the people of Fuzhou feared and asked to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He beat the drum himself, led forty men to smash the barrier within the hour, and Fuzhou surrendered in fear.

sentences.zh: 進攻壽春，天澤獨當一面，宋兵夜出斫營，天澤手擊殺數人，麾下兵繼至，悉驅其兵入淮水死，乘勝而南，所向輒克。

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Shouchun, Tianze alone held one face; Song troops came out by night to raid the camp; Tianze with his hand struck and killed several men; troops under his command followed; all drove the enemy into the Huai to die; following victory he went south and wherever he went he took it.
translations.idiomatic: At Shouchun he held one sector alone; when the Song raided by night he killed several men himself, his troops drove the rest into the Huai, and he swept south taking every objective.

sentences.zh: 壬子，入覲，憲宗賜衛州五城為分邑。

translations.literal: In the renzi year he had audience; Emperor Xianzong granted five cities of Weizhou as a fief.
translations.idiomatic: In renzi he attended court; Möngke granted him five cities in Weizhou as a fief.

sentences.zh: 世祖時在藩邸，極知漢地不治，河南尤甚，請以天澤為經略使。

translations.literal: When Shizu was still in his princely residence he knew well that the Han territories were poorly governed, Henan especially; he asked that Tianze be made commissioner for planning.
translations.idiomatic: While Kublai was still a prince he knew the Han lands were mismanaged, especially Henan, and appointed Tianze to rectify them.

sentences.zh: 至則興利除害，政無不舉，誅郡邑長貳之尤貪橫者二人，境內大治。

translations.literal: When he arrived he promoted profit and removed harm; nothing in government was not carried out; he executed two prefectural and county chiefs who were especially greedy and overbearing; within the borders there was great order.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted what benefited the people and abolished abuses, executed two grossly corrupt local officials, and brought the region to order.

sentences.zh: 阿藍荅兒鉤較諸路財賦，鍛鍊羅織，無所不至，天澤以勳舊獨見優容，天澤曰：「我為經略使，今不我責，而罪餘人，我何安乎！」

translations.literal: Alandai'er audited finances of all routes, forging charges and framing people without limit; Tianze alone as an old merit-holder received preferential treatment; Tianze said, "I am the commissioner—if I am not held responsible but others are blamed, how can I be at ease!"
translations.idiomatic: Alandai'er audited every circuit's finances with endless frame-ups; though Tianze was spared as an old servant, he said, "I am the commissioner—if others are punished in my place, how can I rest?"

sentences.zh: 由是得釋者甚衆。

translations.literal: Thereby very many were released.
translations.idiomatic: Many were released because of him.

sentences.zh: 戊午秋，從憲宗伐宋，由西蜀以入。

translations.literal: In autumn of the wuwu year he followed Emperor Xianzong in attacking the Song, entering by western Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuwu autumn he followed Möngke's Song campaign through western Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 己未夏，駐合州之釣魚山，軍中大疫，方議班師，宋將呂文德以艨艟千餘，泝嘉陵江而上，北軍迎戰不利。

translations.literal: In summer of the jiwei year they encamped at Diaoyushan in Hezhou; the army had a great epidemic; just as they discussed withdrawing, Song general Lü Wende with more than a thousand tower ships went up the Jialing; the northern army met them in battle unfavorably.
translations.idiomatic: In jiwei summer, encamped at Diaoyu in Hezhou during a plague, as withdrawal was debated Lü Wende brought a thousand warships up the Jialing and the Mongols met a reverse.

sentences.zh: 帝命天澤禦之，乃分軍為兩翼，跨江注射，親率舟師順流縱擊，三戰三捷，奪其戰艦百餘艘，追至重慶而還。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Tianze to resist; he divided the army into two wings, shot across the river, personally led the fleet downstream in a running attack, three battles and three victories, seized more than a hundred of their warships, pursued to Chongqing and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai ordered Tianze to meet them; he split his force, fired across the river, led the fleet downstream, won three engagements, took a hundred warships, and pursued to Chongqing.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，世祖即位，首召天澤，問以治國安民之道，即具疏以對，大略謂：「朝廷當先立省部以正紀綱，設監司以督諸路，霈恩澤以安反側，退貪殘以任賢能，頒奉秩以養廉，禁賄賂以防奸，庶能上下丕應，內外休息。」

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, when Shizu took the throne he first summoned Tianze and asked the way to govern the state and settle the people; Tianze immediately submitted a memorial in reply, in general saying, "The court should first establish ministries and departments to correct discipline, set supervisory offices to oversee all routes, spread grace to settle those who had turned away, remove the greedy and cruel and employ the worthy, issue salaries to nurture integrity, forbid bribes to prevent treachery—then above and below may respond and inside and outside rest."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongtong, newly enthroned, Kublai summoned Tianze and asked how to govern; Tianze's memorial urged ministries to set discipline, censors to oversee circuits, amnesty for rebels, removal of the cruel, salaries for integrity, and an end to bribery.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved every point.

sentences.zh: 繼命往鄂渚撤江上軍，還，授河南等路宣撫使，俄兼江淮諸翼軍馬經略使。

translations.literal: He was next ordered to go to Ezhou to withdraw troops on the river; on return he was appointed Pacification Commissioner of Henan and other circuits, soon also Commissioner for Planning the Armies of the Jiang-Huai wings.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent to withdraw the river armies at Ezhou, then made pacification commissioner of Henan and planner of the Jiang-Huai forces.

sentences.zh: 二年夏五月，拜中書右丞相。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer of the second year he was appointed Right Chancellor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year he became right chancellor of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天澤既秉政，凡前所言治國安民之術，無不次第舉行。

translations.literal: Once Tianze held power, every item he had spoken of for governing the state and settling the people was carried out in order without exception.
translations.idiomatic: In office he enacted every reform he had proposed.

sentences.zh: 又定省規十條，以正庶務。

translations.literal: He also fixed ten regulations for the secretariat to correct routine affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He codified ten secretariat regulations.

sentences.zh: 憲宗初年，括戶餘百萬，至是，諸色占役者太半，天澤悉奏罷之。

translations.literal: In the early years of Emperor Xianzong more than a million households had been registered; by this time those occupying corvée in various categories were more than half; Tianze memorialized to abolish them all.
translations.idiomatic: Half the registered households were pressed into miscellaneous corvée since Möngke's census; Tianze had these abolished.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，扈從世祖親征阿里不哥，次昔木土之地，詔丞相線真將右軍，天澤將左軍，合勢蹙之，阿里不哥敗走。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of autumn he accompanied Shizu in the personal campaign against Ariq Böke, halted at Ximutu; the emperor ordered Chancellor Xianzhen to command the right wing and Tianze the left; combining forces they pressed him; Ariq Böke was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he accompanied Kublai against Ariq Böke at Ximutu; Xianzhen commanded the right wing, Tianze the left; Ariq Böke was beaten and fled.

sentences.zh: 三年春，李璮陰結宋人，以益都叛，遂據濟南，詔親王哈必赤緫兵討之，凶勢甚盛。

translations.literal: In spring of the third year Li Tan secretly joined the Song; with Yidu he rebelled and then held Jinan; an edict ordered Prince Hapichi to command troops to suppress; the ferocious momentum was very strong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third spring Li Tan allied with the Song, seized Yidu, then Jinan; Prince Hapichi was sent against him with daunting force.

sentences.zh: 繼命天澤往，天澤聞璮入濟南，笑曰：「豕突入苙，無能為也。」

translations.literal: Tianze was next ordered to go; when he heard Tan had entered Jinan he laughed, "A pig has burst into the pen—he can do nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Tianze was sent after him; hearing Tan had shut himself in Jinan, he laughed, "A pig in a sty—he cannot last."

sentences.zh: 至則進說於哈必赤曰：「璮多譎而兵精，不宜力角，當以歲月斃之。」

translations.literal: When he arrived he advanced counsel to Hapichi, "Tan is treacherous and his troops are skilled; it is not fitting to match strength—he should be worn down over months."
translations.idiomatic: He told Hapichi, "Tan is cunning and his men are skilled—do not fight him head-on; starve him out."

sentences.zh: 乃深溝高壘，絕其奔軼，凡四月，城中食盡，軍潰出降，生擒璮，斬于軍門，誅同惡者數十人，餘悉縱歸。

translations.literal: He then dug deep trenches and built high ramparts, cutting off their breakout; in four months food in the city was exhausted, the army collapsed and came out to surrender; Tan was captured alive and beheaded at the army gate; several tens of co-evildoers were executed; the rest were all released to return.
translations.idiomatic: He entrenched, cut off escape, and after four months starved Jinan into surrender; Li Tan was beheaded, dozens of ringleaders executed, the rest sent home.

sentences.zh: 明日，引軍東行，未至益都，城中人已開門迎降。

translations.literal: The next day he led the army east; before reaching Yidu the people in the city had opened the gates to welcome surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he marched east; before he reached Yidu the city had already opened its gates.

sentences.zh: 初，天澤將行，帝臨軒授詔，責以專征，俾諸將皆聽節度。

translations.literal: Earlier when Tianze was about to go, the emperor at the hall granted an edict, charging him with sole command, ordering all generals to obey his direction.
translations.idiomatic: Before he left, Kublai had given him sole command over all generals.

sentences.zh: 天澤未嘗以詔示人，及還，帝慰勞之，悉歸功於諸將，其慎密謙退如此。

translations.literal: Tianze had never shown the edict to others; when he returned the emperor comforted him; he attributed everything to the generals—his caution, secrecy, and modesty were thus.
translations.idiomatic: He never flaunted that edict; on his return he credited the generals alone—such was his discretion.

sentences.zh: 天澤在憲宗時嘗奏：「臣始攝先兄天倪軍民之職，天倪有二子，一子管民政，一子掌兵權，臣復入叨寄遇，一門之內，處三要職，分所當辭，臣可退休矣。」

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xianzong Tianze had once memorialized, "Your servant first took charge of my late brother Tianni's military and civil duties; Tianni had two sons—one managed civil affairs, one held military power; your servant again received favor—within one gate three key posts; what ought to be divided I should resign; your servant can retire."
translations.idiomatic: Under Möngke he had asked to retire, noting that he, his nephews, and his brother's sons held civil and military power in one clan.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「卿奕世忠勤，有勞於國，一門三職，何愧何嫌！」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "Your clan has been loyal through generations with labor for the state—three posts in one gate, what shame or suspicion!"
translations.idiomatic: Möngke refused: "Your house has served faithfully for generations—why be ashamed of three offices?"

sentences.zh: 竟不許。

translations.literal: In the end it was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 至是，言者或謂李璮之變，由諸侯權太重。

translations.literal: By this time some said Li Tan's rebellion was because the princes' power was too heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Now some blamed Li Tan's revolt on over-mighty regional lords.

sentences.zh: 天澤遂奏：「兵民之權，不可併於一門，行之請自臣家始。」

translations.literal: Tianze then memorialized, "Military and civil power must not rest in one gate; let the practice begin with my family."
translations.idiomatic: Tianze memorialized that civil and military authority must not rest in one clan—and asked to begin with his own.

sentences.zh: 於是史氏子姪，即日解兵符者十七人。

translations.literal: Thereupon seventeen of the Shi clan's sons and nephews that day surrendered their military tallies.
translations.idiomatic: That day seventeen Shi kinsmen surrendered their command tallies.

sentences.zh: 十年春，與平章阿朮等進攻樊城，拔之，襄陽降。

translations.literal: In the tenth spring he with Pacification Commissioner Azhu and others advanced to attack Fancheng, took it, and Xiangyang surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth spring he and Azhu took Fancheng; Xiangyang surrendered.

sentences.zh: 十一年，詔天澤與丞相伯顏緫大軍，自襄陽水陸並進。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year an edict ordered Tianze and Chancellor Bayan to command the great army, from Xiangyang advancing together by water and land.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he and Bayan were ordered to lead the main army from Xiangyang by land and water.

sentences.zh: 天澤至郢州遇疾，還襄陽，帝遣侍臣賜以葡萄酒，且諭之曰：「卿自朕祖宗以來，躬擐甲冑，跋履山川，宣力多矣。

translations.literal: Tianze reached Yingzhou and fell ill, returned to Xiangyang; the emperor sent attendants to bestow grape wine and moreover instructed him, "From the time of my ancestors you have yourself borne armor, traversed mountains and rivers, and exerted strength in many ways.
translations.idiomatic: At Yingzhou he fell ill and returned to Xiangyang; Kublai sent wine and a message: "Since my forefathers' day you have borne armor and crossed mountains in our service.

sentences.zh: 又卿首事南伐，異日功成，皆卿力也。

translations.literal: Moreover you were the first to undertake the southern campaign; when success comes another day, it will all be your strength.
translations.idiomatic: You opened the southern war—when it succeeds, the credit will be yours.

sentences.zh: 勿以小疾阻行為憂，可且北歸，善自調護。」

translations.literal: Do not let a small illness block your going as a worry—you may return north for now and take good care of yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Do not let a minor illness trouble you—go north and recover."

sentences.zh: 還至真定，帝又遣其子杠與尚醫馳視，賜以藥餌。

translations.literal: Returning to Zhending, the emperor again sent his son Gang and the imperial physician in a rush to visit and bestow medicines.
translations.idiomatic: Back at Zhending, Kublai sent his son Gang and the court physician with medicines.

sentences.zh: 天澤因附奏曰：「臣大限有終，死不足惜，但願天兵渡江，慎勿殺掠。」

translations.literal: Tianze therefore appended a memorial saying, "Your servant's great limit has an end; death is not worth grieving; I only wish that when the heavenly army crosses the Yangtze they be careful not to slaughter and plunder."
translations.idiomatic: He added a final memorial: "I am near my end; I only beg that when the army crosses the Yangtze it spare the people from slaughter and looting."

sentences.zh: 語不及它。

translations.literal: His words did not touch on other matters.
translations.idiomatic: He said nothing else.

sentences.zh: 以十二年二月七日薨，年七十四。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the second month of the twelfth year he died; he was seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the second month of the twelfth year he died, aged seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，帝震悼，遣近臣賻以白金二千五百兩，贈太尉，諡忠武。

translations.literal: When the death report arrived the emperor was shaken and grieved; he sent close attendants to grant two thousand five hundred taels of white gold for funeral gifts; he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the posthumous name Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: Kublai mourned him, sent two thousand five hundred taels of silver for the funeral, and posthumously named him Grand Preceptor Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 後累贈太師，進封鎮陽王，立廟。

translations.literal: Later he was repeatedly enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor, advanced to Prince of Zhenyang, and a temple was established.
translations.idiomatic: He was later raised to grand preceptor, enfeoffed as Prince of Zhenyang, and given a temple.

sentences.zh: 天澤平居，未嘗自矜其能，及臨大節、論大事，毅然以天下之重自任。

translations.literal: In ordinary times Tianze never boasted of his ability; yet facing great principle and discussing great affairs he resolutely took the weight of the realm upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: In daily life he never boasted, yet in great affairs he shouldered the realm's weight.

sentences.zh: 年四十，始折節讀書，尤熟於資治通鑑，立論多出人意表。

translations.literal: At forty he first bent his will to read books and was especially versed in the Zizhi Tongjian; his established opinions often went beyond people's expectations.
translations.idiomatic: At forty he took up reading, especially the Zizhi Tongjian, and his judgments often surprised others.

sentences.zh: 拜相之日，門庭悄然，或勸以權自張，天澤舉唐韋澳告周墀之語曰：「願相公無權。

translations.literal: On the day he became chancellor his gate was silent; some urged him to expand power for himself; Tianze cited Tang Wei Ao's words to Zhou Chi, "I wish the minister would have no power.
translations.idiomatic: The day he became chancellor his gate was quiet; when urged to seize power he quoted Wei Ao: "I wish the chancellor had no power.

sentences.zh: 爵祿刑賞，天子之柄，何以權為！」

translations.literal: Rank, salary, punishment, and reward are the Son of Heaven's handles—why make them into power!"
translations.idiomatic: Ranks, salaries, punishments, and rewards belong to the emperor—why call them 'power'?"

sentences.zh: 因以謝之，言者慚服。

translations.literal: He therefore declined; the speakers were ashamed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He declined; his critics withdrew abashed.

sentences.zh: 當金末，名士流寓失所，悉為治其生理而賓禮之，後多致顯達。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jin, famous scholars who had lost their places were all provided for in livelihood and received as guests with ceremony; many later attained high prominence.
translations.idiomatic: At the Jin collapse he sheltered displaced scholars, entertained them honorably, and many later rose high.

sentences.zh: 破歸德，釋李大節不殺，而送至真定，署為參謀。

translations.literal: When Guide was taken he released Li Dajie without killing him and sent him to Zhending, appointing him as staff adviser.
translations.idiomatic: At Guide he spared Li Dajie and made him an adviser at Zhending.

sentences.zh: 衛為食邑，命王昌齡治之，舊人多不平，而莫能間，其知人之明、用人之專如此。

translations.literal: Wei was his fief; he ordered Wang Changling to govern it; old retainers were mostly discontented yet none could sow division—his clarity in knowing men and singleness in employing them were thus.
translations.idiomatic: He put Wang Changling in charge of his Wei fief despite old retainers' jealousy—such was his eye for talent.

sentences.zh: 是以出入將相五十年，上不疑而下無怨，人以比於郭子儀、曹彬云。

translations.literal: Therefore for fifty years entering and leaving as general and minister, the sovereign did not doubt and subordinates did not resent; men compared him to Guo Ziyi and Cao Bin.
translations.idiomatic: For fifty years as general and minister he won the throne's trust and his men's loyalty; posterity compared him to Guo Ziyi and Cao Bin.

sentences.zh: 子格，湖廣行省平章政事；

translations.literal: Son Ge, Pacification Commissioner of the Huguang Branch Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: His son Ge, pacification commissioner of Huguang;

sentences.zh: 樟，真定順天新軍萬戶；

translations.literal: Zhang, commander of ten thousand households of the Zhending-Shuntian New Army;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang, commander of the Zhending-Shuntian new army;

sentences.zh: 棣，衛輝路轉運使；

translations.literal: Di, Transport Commissioner of Weihui Circuit;
translations.idiomatic: Di, transport commissioner of Weihui;

sentences.zh: 杠，湖廣行省右丞；

translations.literal: Gang, Right Vice Director of the Huguang Branch Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: and Gang, right vice director of the Huguang secretariat;

sentences.zh: 杞，淮東道廉訪使；

translations.literal: Qi, Intendant of Surveillance for the Huaidong Circuit;
translations.idiomatic: Qi, intendant of surveillance for Huaidong;

sentences.zh: 梓，同知澧州；

translations.literal: Zi, Associate Prefect of Lizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Zi, associate prefect of Lizhou;

sentences.zh: 楷，同知南陽府；

translations.literal: Kai, Associate Prefect of Nanyang Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Kai, associate prefect of Nanyang;

sentences.zh: 彬，中書左丞。

translations.literal: Bin, Left Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: and Bin, left vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 格字晉明。

translations.literal: Ge, courtesy name Jinming.
translations.idiomatic: Ge, whose courtesy name was Jinming.

sentences.zh: 歲壬子，憲宗賜天澤以衛城，授格節度使。

translations.literal: In the renzi year Emperor Xianzong granted Tianze the city of Wei; Ge was appointed Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In renzi Möngke granted Tianze the city of Wei and made Ge its military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 憲宗崩，格北留謙州，五年而歸，為鄧州舊軍萬戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong died Ge remained north at Qianzhou; after five years he returned and became commander of ten thousand households of the old Dengzhou army.
translations.idiomatic: After Möngke's death Ge stayed five years in Qianzhou, then returned as commander of the old Dengzhou ten-thousand-household unit.

sentences.zh: 既又代張弘範為亳州萬戶，而以故所將鄧州舊軍授弘範。

translations.literal: He next replaced Zhang Hongfan as commander of ten thousand households of Bozhou, and the old Dengzhou army he had led was given to Hongfan.
translations.idiomatic: He then succeeded Zhang Hongfan at Bozhou, trading his Dengzhou command for Hongfan's post.

sentences.zh: 從攻襄陽，襄陽下，賜白金、衣裘、弓矢、鞍馬。

translations.literal: He followed the attack on Xiangyang; when Xiangyang fell he was granted white gold, fur coats, bow and arrows, saddle and horse.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangyang's fall he was rewarded with silver, furs, bow, arrows, saddle, and horse.

sentences.zh: 衆軍渡江，平章阿朮將二十萬戶居前，每五萬戶擇一人為帥統之，格居其一。

translations.literal: When the mass of armies crossed the river, Pacification Commissioner Azhu led two hundred thousand households in the van; for every fifty thousand households one man was chosen as commander to rule them—Ge was one of these.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing the Yangtze under Azhu, every fifty thousand households were placed under one commander—Ge held one such command.

sentences.zh: 格軍先渡，為宋將程鵬飛所却，格被三創，喪其師二百，尋復大戰，中流矢，鵬飛身亦被七創，乃敗走。

translations.literal: Ge's army crossed first and was repulsed by Song general Cheng Pengfei; Ge received three wounds and lost two hundred of his division; soon they fought again greatly; he was struck by a flowing arrow; Pengfei's person also received seven wounds; he then was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ge crossed first, was beaten back by Cheng Pengfei with three wounds and two hundred dead; in a rematch both were wounded—Pengfei seven times, Ge by an arrow—and the Song fled.

sentences.zh: 其後樞密院奏格輕進，請罪之，帝念其功，而薄其罪。

translations.literal: Afterward the Secretariat for Military Affairs memorialized that Ge had advanced rashly and asked to punish him; the emperor remembered his merit and lightened the crime.
translations.idiomatic: The military secretariat asked to punish his rash advance; the emperor pardoned him for past service.

sentences.zh: 俾從平章阿里海牙攻潭州，砲激柵木，傷肩，矢貫其手，裹創先登，拔之，遂以軍民安撫留戍。

translations.literal: He was ordered to follow Pacification Commissioner Alihaiya in attacking Tanzhou; catapults shattered the stockade timbers and wounded his shoulder; an arrow pierced his hand; wrapping the wound he was first to ascend and took it; he was then left as pacification commissioner to garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Under Alihaiya at Tanzhou he was wounded by catapult fire and an arrow, yet bandaged his hand and led the escalade; he was left to garrison the city.

sentences.zh: 入覲，加定遠大將軍，賜以天澤所服玉帶。

translations.literal: He had audience and was promoted to Stabilizing-the-Distant Grand General; he was granted the jade belt Tianze had worn.
translations.idiomatic: At court he was made stabilizing-the-distant grand general and given his father's jade belt.

sentences.zh: 從攻靜江，衆以轒轀自蔽鑿城，格所當，砲礌蔽地，車不可至，乃伺隙率衆攀堞，蟻附而上，拔之。

translations.literal: Following the attack on Jingjiang, the mass used covered rams to bore the walls; at Ge's sector cannon stones covered the ground and carts could not reach; he waited for an opening and led the masses climbing the parapet, ant-like attaching upward, and took it.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingjiang, where bombardment blocked the rams, he led men up the walls like ants and took the city.

sentences.zh: 徇廣西十州、廣東三州，皆下。

translations.literal: He overran ten prefectures of Guangxi and three of Guangdong—all fell.
translations.idiomatic: He reduced ten Guangxi prefectures and three in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 靜江受兵之初，溪洞諸夷皆降雲南，格遣使諭之，來者五十州，雲南爭之，事聞，詔聽格節度。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingjiang's suffering from troops, the various Yi of the stream valleys all submitted to Yunnan; Ge sent envoys to instruct them; fifty states came; Yunnan disputed it; the matter was reported; an edict ordered Ge to command.
translations.idiomatic: When stream tribes submitted to Yunnan, Ge won fifty back by envoy; Yunnan protested, but the court left them under his command.

sentences.zh: 陞廣西宣撫使，改鎮國上將軍、廣南西道宣慰使。

translations.literal: He was promoted Pacification Commissioner of Guangxi and changed to Pacifying-the-Realm General and Pacification Commissioner of the Western Guangnan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He became pacification commissioner of Guangxi, then pacifying-the-realm general and pacification commissioner of western Guangnan.

sentences.zh: 宋亡，陳宜中、張世傑挾益王昰、廣王昞據福州，立益王，傳檄嶺海，欲復其地，詐言夏貴已復瀕江州郡。

translations.literal: When the Song perished, Chen Yizhong and Zhang Shijie held the Prince of Yi Zhao and the Prince of Guang Zhao at Fuzhou, established the Prince of Yi, and issued proclamations across the Linghai, wishing to recover their territory, falsely saying Xia Gui had already recovered the river-bank prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After the Song fell, Chen Yizhong and Zhang Shijie set up the boy emperors at Fuzhou and falsely claimed Xia Gui had retaken the Yangtze coast.

sentences.zh: 諸戍將以江路既絕，不可北歸，皆託計事還靜江。

translations.literal: The garrison generals, because the river route was already cut and they could not return north, all pleaded business and returned to Jingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal garrisons, fearing they could not return north, deserted to Jingjiang on pretexts.

sentences.zh: 格曰：「君等亦為虛聲所懼邪！

translations.literal: Ge said, "Are you also frightened by empty rumors!
translations.idiomatic: Ge said, "Are you frightened by rumors too?

sentences.zh: 待貴踰嶺，審不可北歸，吾與諸君取塗雲南而歸，未為不可，敢輒棄戍哉！」

translations.literal: Wait until Gui crosses the ranges; if it is truly impossible to return north, I with you will take the road through Yunnan to return—not impossible; how dare you lightly abandon the garrison!"
translations.idiomatic: If Xia Gui cannot restore the north, we can march home through Yunnan—how dare you abandon your posts!"

sentences.zh: 行省議棄廣東之肇慶、德慶、封州，併兵戍梧州。

translations.literal: The branch secretariat discussed abandoning Zhaoqing, Deqing, and Fengzhou of Guangdong and combining troops to garrison Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The branch secretariat proposed abandoning Zhaoqing, Deqing, and Feng in Guangdong and concentrating at Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 格曰：「棄地撤備，示敵以怯，不可，宜增兵戍之。」

translations.literal: Ge said, "Abandoning territory and withdrawing defense shows the enemy timidity—it cannot be done; troops should be increased to garrison them."
translations.idiomatic: Ge objected: "Evacuation shows fear—we should reinforce those posts."

sentences.zh: 劇賊蘇仲，集潰卒，據鎮龍山稱王，劫掠於外，耕植於內，至秋畢穫。

translations.literal: The fierce bandit Su Zhong gathered scattered troops, held Zhenlong Mountain and called himself king, plundering outside and farming within, until autumn harvest was complete.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Su Zhong crowned himself on Mount Zhenlong, raiding outward and farming within until the harvest.

sentences.zh: 聞大兵至，則偽出降，官軍畏暑，不敢深入，橫、象、賓、貴四州，皆被其害。

translations.literal: Hearing the great army had come he falsely offered surrender; the government troops feared heat and did not penetrate deeply; Heng, Xiang, Bin, and Gui—four prefectures—all suffered from him.
translations.idiomatic: He feigned surrender when troops approached; government forces, fearing the heat, held back, and Heng, Xiang, Bin, and Gui suffered.

sentences.zh: 格築堡於其界，守以土兵，令官軍火其廬柵，民踐其禾稼，仲窮蹙，遂降。

translations.literal: Ge built a fort on his border, garrisoned it with native troops, ordered government troops to burn his huts and stockades, and the people trampled his grain crops; Zhong was pressed to extremity and then submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Ge built border forts, burned Su Zhong's camps, trampled his crops, and forced his surrender.

sentences.zh: 益王餘衆破潯州。

translations.literal: The remaining troops of the Prince of Yi broke Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Remnants of the Yi emperor's faction seized Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 斬李辰、李福。

translations.literal: Li Chen and Li Fu were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chen and Li Fu were executed.

sentences.zh: 靜江北抵全、永，皆城守，羅飛圍永，凡七月不下。

translations.literal: North of Jingjiang to Quan and Yong all held walled defense; Luo Fei besieged Yong—for seven months it would not fall.
translations.idiomatic: From Jingjiang north to Quan and Yong the cities held out; Luo Fei besieged Yong for seven months.

sentences.zh: 判官潘澤民間道來告急，格分兵赴之，殄其衆。

translations.literal: Judge Pan Zemin came by a hidden path to report urgency; Ge divided troops to go; they exterminated his masses.
translations.idiomatic: Judge Pan Zemin slipped through the lines for help; Ge sent relief and destroyed Luo Fei's force.

sentences.zh: 益王死，衛王立。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yi died; the Prince of Wei was established.
translations.idiomatic: The Yi emperor died; the Wei emperor was installed.

sentences.zh: 趣廣州，壁海中崖山，遣曾淵子據雷州，諭之降，不聽，進兵攻之，淵子奔碙洲。

translations.literal: He hastened to Guangzhou; they walled themselves on Yashan in the sea; he sent Zeng Yuanzi to hold Leizhou and instructed surrender; they would not listen; he advanced to attack; Yuanzi fled to Qiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed Guangzhou; the Song held Yamen at sea; his envoy at Leizhou was refused, and Zeng Yuanzi fled to Qiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 世傑將兵數萬，欲復取雷州，戍將劉仲海擊走之。

translations.literal: Shijie led several tens of thousands of troops wishing to retake Leizhou; the garrison general Liu Zhonghai struck and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shijie tried to retake Leizhou with tens of thousands; Liu Zhonghai repulsed him.

sentences.zh: 後悉衆來圍，城中絕糧，士以草為食，格漕欽、廉、高、化諸州糧以給之，世傑解圍去。

translations.literal: Later he led all his masses to besiege; grain in the city was cut off; soldiers ate grass; Ge transported grain from Qin, Lian, Gao, and Hua to supply them; Shijie lifted the siege and left.
translations.idiomatic: When Shijie besieged Leizhou and the garrison ate grass, Ge shipped grain from coastal prefectures and Shijie withdrew.

sentences.zh: 詔格戍雷州。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Ge to garrison Leizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ge was ordered to garrison Leizhou.

sentences.zh: 衛王死，廣東、西悉平。

translations.literal: The Prince of Wei died; Guangdong and Guangxi were entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: After the Wei emperor's death, Guangdong and Guangxi were fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 張弘範請復將亳州軍。

translations.literal: Zhang Hongfan asked to have the Bozhou army restored to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hongfan asked to recover the Bozhou command.

sentences.zh: 乃還格鄧州舊軍。

translations.literal: Ge was then returned the old Dengzhou army.
translations.idiomatic: Ge received back his Dengzhou troops.

sentences.zh: 拜參知政事、行廣南西道宣慰使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Participating in Government Affairs and Acting Pacification Commissioner of the Western Guangnan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was made participating councillor and acting pacification commissioner of western Guangnan.

sentences.zh: 入覲，拜資德大夫、湖廣行中書省右丞。

translations.literal: He had audience and was appointed Worthy-and-Virtuous Grand Master and Right Vice Director of the Huguang Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At court he became worthy-and-virtuous grand master and right vice director of the Huguang secretariat.

sentences.zh: 移江西右丞，尋復為湖廣右丞，進平章政事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Vice Director of Jiangxi, soon again Right Vice Director of Huguang, and advanced to Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as right vice director in Jiangxi, returned to Huguang, and rose to pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: He died; he was fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 子燿，福建行省平章政事；

translations.literal: Son Yao, Pacification Commissioner of the Fujian Branch Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: His son Yao, pacification commissioner of Fujian;

sentences.zh: 榮，鄧州舊軍萬戶。

translations.literal: Rong, commander of ten thousand households of the old Dengzhou army.
translations.idiomatic: and Rong, commander of the old Dengzhou ten-thousand-household unit.
